Colouring: back-and-forth zig-zag hatching with a visible gap, each pass at a slightly different pressure; overshoot the outline by a few px; a lighter cross-hatch pass on big areas.

Watercolour wash: a separate density canvas multiplied over the page. Pigment pools at edges (density minus blurred density), granulates in the deepest pits, blooms with noise, and is resisted by wax (density × (1 − ~0.9·wax coverage)). Brush strokes are wide

Occlusion: a front part erases what is behind it inside its outline; characters "keep the paper white" behind them (a knock-out that restores paper and resets wax), the way a child draws the figure first and colours around it.
colour_logic: A box of about a dozen crayons, never more. Outlines in one dark colour (indigo, dark brown, plum), never black. One white crayon reserved for wax resist.
At most one watercolour per film, chosen for what it reveals (ultramarine for night, rose for dawn, sap green for rain). It never paints the characters.
Saturated crayon on lots of bare paper; value comes from pressure, not extra hues. One accent on a character may echo the story.
Example boxes: *seaside* — navy line, coral, sand, teal, turquoise, lemon, white; *orchard* — brown line, russet, apple red, mustard, olive, plum, cream, white.
motion: Everything drawn steps at 12 fps (lines, colouring, characters, boil seed); camera, the wash's leading edge and twinkles run at 24 fps.

Boil: each stroke re-jitters offset (<1 px), wobble and hatching rows every 2 frames. Characters full, background lines ~0.6, background colouring still (it also halves the bitrate). Calm the boil to about half when the film goes quiet.
Drawing on: lines reveal along their length in 0.4–0.9 s; colouring row by row; text letter by letter.
Acting: substitution, a new drawing per pose on the beat; two key drawings alternate for a repeated action. Big simple poses; a child's drawing doesn't in-between.
Colouring is an action: being coloured in *is* doing (a coat scribbled on = putting it on; pink scribble = blushing; a wash = night falling).
camera_grammar: Held wide while the brush moves
Pull out past the page edge
sound_palette: Small wooden and metal-toothed instruments, no strings or grand piano: ukulele or nylon guitar, clarinet or bassoon (bass, humour), music box (can wind down with a pitch droop), glockenspiel or celesta (a note per uncovered sparkle), toy piano (one note per co
Silence is a beat: a full beat of nothing after a failure; a short breath before a wordless passage.

Foley follows the material: crayon = stick-slip band-passed noise whose grain follows stroke speed (colouring = rhythmic swishes); wet brush = soft low-passed noise with bristle grain, panned with the stroke; felt puffs, fabric swishes, a sharpener, a crayon s
Mix: music under narration, rising for wordless passages; metal voices get a gentle high lift. −14 LUFS.
pitfalls_limits: Gaps between wash bands leave white stripes → overlap bands and cover all intended paper.
Wavy band edges and wide light streaks read as hills → small high-frequency waviness, thin faint streaks (α ≤ 0.12).
Light-pressure colouring goes muddy under a wash → pressure ≥ 0.8 or cross-hatch wherever the wash crosses.
Text where the wash passes survives it (wax resists) → place it elsewhere or accept it.
Characters vanish under a wash → composite them *after* the wash.
Outlines over hair read as a headband → outline hair masses on their outer edge only.
Knock-out drawn into a plain layer shows as grey crayon → use a dummy canvas.
Page turn from rectangle strips shows a staircase → an affine transform per strip.
styles.engine_section: In `demo/`: `gl.js` (WebGL2 compositor: paper, wax adhesion, knock-out, watercolour + resist, emboss/vignette/lamp), `crayon.js` (`line` ribbons with taper, streaks, boil; `fill` hatching with overshoot; `text`; shapes), `rig.js` (occlusion + knock-out parts, limb tubes), `sheet.js` (model sheets, `?test=model&page=…`), `end.js` (page on a desk, page turn). Draw your own character's model sheet with them before any shot. File map and commands: [DEMO.md](DEMO.md#build-notes).

styles.name: Chinese Ink Wash
styles.official_demo_line: A swordsman crosses the river on the water and splits the current with a single stroke.
styles.principles: An ink painting (水墨) painted and unrolled before you: black ink on warm rice paper in five tones, plus one red, the vermilion seal. No Western outlines: forms are made by loaded brushstrokes whose dark edge *is* the contour (没骨, "boneless" painting), by wet washes that bleed into the paper, and by dry, fast strokes where the paper shows through the bristle tracks (飞白, "flying white").
construction: Paper is procedural, in the compositor, never a texture file: warm rice paper (around `#F2ECDE`), cloud mottling, long fibres, pulp flecks, grain that fades when zoomed out (or it shimmers), a light vignette; anchored to the world.
Ink is stroke opacity multiplied onto paper (never an overlay), in five tones (墨分五色):

Brushstroke model: centreline × pressure profile × width noise, plus 4–60 bristles whose ink load drops along the stroke and breaks on long-scale noise. `dry` runs from a solid wet stroke to flying white (dry strokes are bristle tracks only).
Loaded stroke: bristles darker on one side, so the stroke carries its own contour: this makes bodies, rocks and waves read as ink, not vectors.
Two layers: the wet one bleeds in the compositor (noisy blur, edge pigment accumulation, granulation); the dry one only gets fibre jitter and paper tooth.
Masses: soft polygons, jittered edges, a gradient; never flat fills.
colour_logic: Ink only, from cool grey at low density to warm black at full density. No other hue in the world.

One vermilion (around `#B02E22`), for the seal and at most one tiny accent in the story (an object the protagonist carries). The accent finds the protagonist in wide shots and can rhyme with the seal. Never a red wash, never red type.
Values carry depth: far = pale and soft, near = dark and textured. If a frame gets busy, remove ink rather than add tone.
motion: Figures step at 12 fps (on twos); their position, the camera, blooms, ripples and splatter move on ones at 24 fps.

Stable strokes on twos: seed every stroke by its index and compute bristle breaks along *normalized* arc length × a fixed reference length, so flying-white gaps don't crawl every drawing. Allow only a small "boil" on the width noise.
Painted into existence: strokes appear in drawing order.

Stillness before action (when a decisive stroke is the event): hold, with at most a slow push-in, then let the stroke cross the frame in a few frames. Consequences start only after the stroke has finished.
Nothing is tweened like a vector shape: things are painted, bloom or dissolve into mist.
camera_grammar: Lateral tracking, lead room, slow far parallax
High wide, a tiny figure in blank paper
Low angle, dark mass towering, slow push-in with shake
Hard cut to an extreme close-up
Push into an ink bloom or mist
Pull back until a mark joins the whole
sound_palette: Guqin-led, not piano and strings: guqin (`core/audio/pluck.py` `guqin`: open and stopped strings, slides, vibrato, glassy harmonics, sweeps), a low breathy xiao, big drum and timpani for mass, frame drum for steps, a small gong for a seal. Chinese pentatonic m
Cue to the picture, never loop: unmetred plucks suit emptiness, a pulse suits movement, rolls suit mass; painted strokes can each land on a pluck.
Silence is literal: zero the whole bus (music, ambience, reverb tails) with short fades. At most one sound inside it (a drip, one ring). Place it where the story holds its breath.

Foley follows the material: ink drop (short "tink" + soft wet thud), brush air (band-passed noise with bristle grains, never a metal whoosh), steps on water (small splash), splatter (wet ticks), seal (wooden thump + paper crackle).
pitfalls_limits: Dry brush looks like dashed lines → breaks from long-scale noise and an ink load that drops along the stroke.
Parallel semi-transparent strokes make bodies look like organ pipes → one base mass + two loaded strokes.
Big side-brush strokes look like a hairbrush → a gradient mass + a few low-dryness strokes. Gradients in vertical bands leave seams → a cached per-pixel layer.
A stroke body split between wet and dry layers loses density → full body in the dry layer plus a wet halo.
Clipping calligraphy with the font outline notches the junctions → font as skeleton only.
Uniform hatching inside a wave turns it into a wire mesh → loaded strokes along the face.
styles.engine_section: In `demo/`: `ink.js` (brush engine: strokes, bristles, loaded strokes, masses, blots), `comp.js` (WebGL rice-paper compositor: bleed, edge pigment, paper, bloom), `land.js` (mountains, cun, cliffs, pine, reeds, ripples), `wave.js` (gestural wave), `glyph.js` (skeleton-traced calligraphy), `seal.js` (vermilion seal), `hero.js` (xieyi figure rig), `subs.js` (inscription subtitles), `music/score.py` (guqin writing with `core/audio/pluck.py`); `?test=sheet|pose|frame` pages draw model sheets from the real engine.

styles.name: Ukiyo-e
styles.official_demo_line: A traveller walks toward a distant mountain; every shot is a woodblock print, a great wave at the climax, the mountain and the whole scroll at the end.
styles.principles: Every shot is a complete woodblock print: a sheet of washi, a thin double ink border, flat areas of colour printed from separate blocks, a black key-block line on top, a vertical title cartouche and a red seal. The world is flat on purpose. Depth comes from stacked horizontal layers, mist bands and bold cropping, never from perspective rendering, lighting or shading.
construction: The sheet is the frame: the print fills the screen at zoom 1, inside a thick + thin ink border, with a paper margin beyond. Sheets can sit on a long mounting scroll (darker tan paper, a roller at one end), so the camera can travel from print to print.

Blocks: draw each colour group into its own offscreen canvas, cached once (key lines; blues; greens / secondary; reds / figures). Composite each with a small fixed registration offset (1.5–2.5 px, a different direction per block).

Texture every colour block: woodgrain (`source-atop`, strongest in sky and water) → baren streaks → goma-zuri specks (both `destination-out`); the key block gets specks only; light paper fibres over the finished sheet so paper shows through the ink. Big dynami
Bokashi is generated per pixel: a gradient whose top edge wanders by low-frequency noise per column (±20–30 px). Never strips of `fillRect` (vertical seams).
Line: key lines 2.4–3 px; large contours are variable-width filled strokes, tapered at both ends, with ±20–35 % low-frequency width jitter. Distant things get a grey key line or none.

Motifs of the medium: mist as long rounded flat bands (suyari-gasumi) fading at both ends; pines with flat-topped needle pads; fields as high, flat, parallel layers whose cross lines are parallel and slanted, never converging; rain as two sets of fine straight
colour_logic: A pigment set, not a colour wheel: 6–9 flat hues, each printed from its own block, over the paper ground. No gradients except bokashi, no shading on forms.
Sumi key line over everything; paper is the white (no white pigment for foam, snow, mist, blank sky).
One dominant hue family carries sky and water (in the 19th-century prints, Prussian blue); red is rare: seals, a sun, one garment or tab.
Far layers pale and low-contrast, near layers saturated with dark key lines.
motion: Prints are still. Most of the frame does not move; each view has one or two small actions (steam, rain, a lantern, a falling leaf).
Figures and nature step at 8 fps; rain and fast water at 12 fps; the camera moves on ones (24 fps). A stepped camera judders.
Printing reveal: each block appears over ~0.3 s with a diagonal baren sweep with a noisy edge, sliding 5–6 px into registration as it lands (pure noise looks like mould).
Cartouches drop in (fade + a short slide); a seal *stamps* (scale ~1.35 → 1 in 0.2 s).
A native move needs a held beat of about a second to be read; a peak flashed in under a second reads as noise.
camera_grammar: Handscroll slide, right → left through the mounting gap (shorter slides = urgency)
Very slow push toward a framing device (a window, a fan, a gate)
Tilt past the border into the mount
Pull-back from one sheet to many
Crash-zoom into the texture (grain, specks, fibres)
Pan across a triptych (three sheets side by side)
Hard cut to a blank sheet
sound_palette: Japanese instruments, not piano and pads: shamisen (`core/audio/pluck.py shamisen`, with sawari buzz), shakuhachi, koto, taiko and shime-daiko, kotsuzumi / ōtsuzumi calls, hyōshigi (wooden clappers), a small bell.
Modes: miyako-bushi (in scale), yō, ritsu; long breathy tones with a slide into each note and *meri* drops at phrase ends suit the shakuhachi; the shamisen can hold a pulse or an ostinato.

Techniques, as options: absolute silence as *ma* (cut reverb tails too); a single sawari note left ringing; free-rhythm breath phrases against a steady pulse; clappers that accelerate (the kabuki curtain call); a taiko heartbeat that tightens into a roll; a ko

Foley follows the material: paper (baren rub = band-passed noise with a slow circular modulation; scroll slide; seal = low thump + tacky peel), wood (block set down, hollow steps), glass (wind chime), water, birds and insects of the season.
pitfalls_limits: Bokashi from `fillRect` strips leaves vertical seams → build it per pixel.
Too much speckle or fibre makes dark areas look like sandpaper or scratched film → specks α ≈ 0.3, fibres α ≈ 0.09.
A perspective grid for fields looks digital → parallel, slanted, flat layering.
Pine clusters drawn as half-discs look like parasols → flat pads with needle fans.
Offset curves self-intersect at tight bends → build inner lines from the gentle side of the contour; force control points x-monotonic.
Breaking out of the print must escape both the sheet clip and the frame clip.
A seal drawn with `multiply` vanishes on dark ground → `source-over` there.
styles.engine_section: In `demo/`: `print.js` (paper, woodgrain, baren, specks, blocks, bokashi, carved lines, reveal masks, cartouche, seals: the reusable core), `nature.js` (mountains, pines, rocks, rain, birds), `wave.js` (banded water, fractal claws, spray), `traveler.js` (flat figure rig), `views.js` (prints as cached blocks + per-frame `paint()`), `main.js` (camera, scroll, reveal, subtitles), `music/score.py`. Instrument recipes and commands: [DEMO.md](DEMO.md#build-notes).

styles.name: Paper-cut Lightbox
styles.official_demo_line: An old night train makes its last run, from a snowy mountain halt through a long tunnel to the sea, its lit windows going out one by one at the end of the line.
styles.principles: Every shot is made of one physical object: a shallow box (a cavity about 0.56 × 0.33 m, 0.16 m deep) holding parallel sheets of cut paper. Two framings are both valid, and a film may use either or both: box framing (the lamp's edge or frame is in the picture) and full-bleed (the lens is inside the box and the paper scenery fills the screen). The stack, the backlight and the shadows are the same in both. Everything on screen is one of three things:
construction: Units in metres, y up. Layers from z ≈ −0.14 (sky) to 0 (front); camera at z ≈ 0.2–0.56, fov ~26°. In box framing, sheets are never larger than the cavity. In full-bleed shots that travel, a layer may be a long strip that scrolls past, and the sky panel moves

A layer is a Canvas2D drawing in metre space mapped to a plane; cut-outs are `destination-out` holes. Finish on every sheet: fibre grain (`source-atop`), a warm top rim and a dark bottom shade, each shifted a few px.

Backlight shader: `emissive += albedo × lightCol × trans × lit × falloff × (base + cloud)`, with a Gaussian falloff around a per-shot light point and a tiled pulp-mottle texture. `trans` per layer goes from ~.9 (far) to ~.05 (front).
Emissive windows: a second canvas (white = light) gated by a 0→1 "switch on" uniform; bloom makes them burn. Titles, lights and curtains in front neither cast nor receive shadows.
Lens: shallow depth of field, bloom, a gentle vignette; supersample 2× so cut edges stay crisp.
Real-world set (when used): wood frame, black lining, a dark room, an area light as the box's spill onto real objects.
colour_logic: Back layers bright and translucent, front layers dark and opaque. Each layer is one flat colour; the ladder of values from back to front is the depth. Never break it (a pale front layer flattens the box).
One temperature per stack, chosen by the scene (cool night, warm interior, violet or green elsewhere). Changing ladder is how the film says "another place".
Light is warm (amber to gold) against the stack, and it is the only saturated element besides one accent.
One accent colour (a seal red, or a single object's colour) marks what the story is about. A second accent only when the story has two sides (one each).
motion: Everything moves like paper on a stick: layers slide (x/y), rotate about a pivot, scale in from 0 along one axis ("written out"), or light up. No squash and stretch, no morphing, no bending.

Figures are optional. A film can tell its story with lit windows, vehicles, lamps and objects, and have no figure at all. When it has figures, they are jointed silhouettes: a body sheet + separate limb sheets anchored at the joint; animate rotation only.
Light cues are the big motion: the source, then each layer's translucency in a ~0.4 s stagger, then windows, then flicker (`1 + .06·sin(7.3t)·sin(3.1t)`).
Hard action lands on spoken words (use whisper word timings): an object slams, a character flashes, a light arc grows on its word.
Hand-held micro-drift on the camera (~0.6 mm) keeps a locked frame alive. Render on ones at 30 fps; never step.
camera_grammar: Pull out of / push into the box
Locked frame with only light changing
sound_palette: Instruments that sit like light behind paper: felt piano, music box, celesta, harp or plucked zithers, bamboo flutes, soft strings; a solo instrument of the topic's culture. No drum kit; percussion only as single soft strokes (woodblock, small gong, hand drum)

Foley is paper and light: switch click + rising shimmer when a light turns on; paper rustle and slide; card-stock tap; lid thud; chimes on reveals; soft whoosh for curtains; beds from the scene (river, rails, city hum, crickets, snow wind).
Silence: the lamp switched off — all sound but a room tone drops out, then returns with the light.
Mix character: voice compressed and forward (RMS ~−18 dB), music underneath with ~5–6 dB of ducking under speech, foley low (−24…−34 dB), peak-limited, final at −14 LUFS.
native_moves: Light burst from an opened thing.
pitfalls_limits: `destination-out` cut-outs need an opaque fillStyle before punching, or the hole is half-cut (`world.js` `cut(x, fn)` does it).
Soft shadows bleed and halo: layers that must not take part need both `shadow: false` and `recv: false`.
A transparent radial-gradient texture shows a square edge as an additive glow → use an analytic shader falloff (`burst()`).
A near-plane curtain whose halves don't meet at their front edges leaves a slit of the old shot.
Sheets larger than the cavity poke through the frame in outside shots.

Grade state must not carry over between shots: every grade key a shot omits must fall back to a default each frame, or renders depend on which frame a worker started on (visible pops at worker boundaries).
Light over paper text: a lamp's glow or a headlight flare over a name board or a card washes the letters out. Keep every lit point clear of text.
Subtitles over a lit window lose their contrast: frame so the bottom band is dark, or put the faint band behind them.
styles.engine_section: In `demo/src/`: `paper.js` (`sheet()` = one lit paper layer with an optional glow map and reveal uniforms; `skyPanel`, `moon`, `text`, `burst`), `stage.js` (scene, top spot, backlight uniforms, `aim()` camera), `post.js` (DoF, bloom, transitions, grade), `world.js` (paper motifs: peaks, firs, the train's carriages; the first shot), `shots.js` (the other shots), `lib.js`. `src/main.js` reads one timeline and draws each shot, two during a dissolve; each shot is `build(E) → { S, update(t), post(), grade() }`. API table and a minimal shot: [DEMO.md](DEMO.md) "Engine reference".

styles.name: Liminal Found Footage
styles.official_demo_line: A new night-shift hire films their first night in an endless yellow office, following the rules on the wall.
styles.principles: - One first-person camcorder recording (1990s VHS, 4:3), handheld, continuous. - An empty, familiar-but-wrong interior that repeats: an office, a hotel floor, a school, a mall, a parking level, a hospital wing. Humming fluorescent light, no people. - Dread from emptiness, repetition, bureaucratic rules, and the camera's own machinery failing at the wrong moment. Nothing chases anyone. A chill on the back of the neck, not a jump. - The medium is the storyteller: focus, exposure, tape damage and the on-screen display carry the plot.
construction: Frame: 4:3 pillarboxed in 1920×1080. Render 3D at low resolution (e.g. 720×540) and let the VHS pass upscale; low resolution hides CG cleanliness.

Space: axis-aligned partitions on a grid with random gaps and stubs, pillars, a drop ceiling of tiles with recessed light panels at regular intervals. A hand-authored route through procedurally filled space, so every doorway shows more emptiness.

Lighting = thousands of lights, no shadows: store every panel's colour and intensity in a float texture; each fragment sums the nearest panels (emitter cosine × Lambert / (d² + ε)) plus a bounce term. No occlusion: this light is flat. Per-light variation (a fe

Fog follows local light: fog colour × (local light / average). Where lights are dead the haze is dark, so a silhouette there reads as a *hole in the light*. Background = fog × ~0.15, so corridors dissolve into darkness, never a bright wall.

Restrained decay: tide-marks at the foot of some walls, a discoloured band under the ceiling, rare peeling seams, a few yellowed or missing tiles, dead insects in diffusers. Percentages in single digits.
Printed matter: office laser-print on yellowed paper, condensed sans headers, form numbers and revisions, numbered rules, a polite closing line from "Management". Pinned or taped.
colour_logic: One dominant sickly hue from the location's materials (mustard wallpaper, institutional green, hospital blue, beige laminate), with a darker trim and a mottled floor of the same family; ceiling and light panels near-white and slightly warm.

Exactly one saturated colour: a signal such as a red alarm lamp, a green emergency sign, an amber warning light. It is the only thing that blooms (drive its emissive high enough to cross the bloom threshold).
White balance drifts; colour is never graded clean.

Example material palettes: wallpaper `#d5bd66`, trim `#4d3d26`, carpet `#8c763c`; pool tile `#9fc7c0`, grout `#e6ece6`, water `#5e8f96`; school corridor `#b9c49a`, lockers `#6f7f66`, linoleum `#a89a7d`.
motion: One continuous handheld take. Cuts happen only where the tape breaks: power-on roll-in, tracking tear, REC off.
Handheld = walking gait (head bob a few cm, sway, small roll) + breathing (~0.27 Hz) + tremor noise at a few frequencies whose amplitude follows a fear curve. At a held breath, freeze all of it.
Looking down shows only shoe toes and floor, never legs.
Autofocus = focus distance animated with overshoot: blur → lock → slip → lock. Blur comes from pulling focus *near*. Zoom narrows the FOV and opens the aperture.
Lights flicker as short blackouts (~0.1 s); auto-exposure catches up with a lag (~0.45 s) and gain noise pumps.
Things move by themselves slowly (a door over >1 s, eased), never snap.
camera_grammar: Slow pan off a detail to the space
Crouch and hold on printed text
Zoom + focus hunt into the distance
Identical framing after a tear, only the OSD changed
Camera set down on a surface, static, recording alone
Whip toward a sound, then nothing
sound_palette: No score. Only what the tape would have recorded. Music exists only inside the world (hold music, a radio through walls, a tinny PA jingle), filtered and reverberant, possibly slowing with tape wow.
Fluorescent bed: 120 Hz (or 100 Hz) + harmonics, a buzzy band-passed component, a faint ballast whine, bad-tube bursts; gated by the same light curve as the picture; closer in small rooms.

PA voice: calm, corporate, through a ceiling speaker (band-pass ~300–3500 Hz, cone resonance, saturation, room reverb), dry enough to stay intelligible. A short original chime before announcements; after a time jump, chime and voice may drift flat.
Operator: a few short, quiet lines with proximity bass and breath; breathing whose rate follows fear; a held breath and one long exhale.
native_moves: The thing that is almost human.
pitfalls_limits: A fully bright scene reads as a hospital corridor → partitions with gaps; far areas fall dark.
Lights leak through walls (no occlusion) → a dead zone needs every light within ~±5 m dead, and the space behind it dim.
Background shows as a bright rectangle at a corridor's end → background = fog × ~0.15.
Uniform fog lifts silhouettes to grey → fog follows local light.
Line wobble skews text; pitching down italicises it → ≤ 0.25 px wobble; lower the camera.
Primitive-built figures read as toys, primitive legs as tubes → organic silhouettes; show only shoe toes.
Pure red never blooms at low emissive (low luminance) → drive it far higher.
Normalising a filtered signal by its pre-filter peak blows up a bus → normalise the processed signal.
styles.engine_section: `demo/world.js` (layout, light DataTexture, custom lighting and fog shaders, props), `demo/tex.js` (procedural wallpaper, carpet, ceiling, panels, notices, signs), `demo/vhs.js` (VHS camcorder ShaderPass), `demo/osd.js` (bitmap font, REC, battery, clock, title generator), `demo/subs.js` (608 captions), `demo/thing2d.js` (organic silhouette), `demo/story.js` (timeline, camera keyframes, focus / fear curves, time warp), `demo/main.js` (renderer, post chain GTAO + DOF + bloom → VHS, handheld rig). File map and build: [DEMO.md](DEMO.md#build-notes).

styles.name: Neon Tubes
styles.official_demo_line: A neon cat goes out for the goldfish on the sign at the end of the street, cracks its bowl, and runs the fading fish home through the rain to the goblet on its own sign.
styles.principles: - Glass, not lines. A lit tube reads as a cylinder: a saturated gas column in the bore, a thin glass wall, a highlight along the top, a halo that spills onto whatever is behind. An unlit tube is still visible as clear glass or milky white (phosphor coated). - Real gas colours. Clear glass + neon = red-orange; clear glass + argon and a drop of mercury = blue. Every other colour is a phosphor coating (milky when off). - Built objects. Tubes stand off painted boards on supports with tie wires; strokes are joined by black-painted double-backs; every tube ends in a blacked-out electrode; a transfor
construction: Tube = centreline polyline in metres (`lib.js tubeFromStrokes`): corners filleted with a radius of about one tube diameter, strokes joined by painted double-backs, painted sleeves and an electrode cap at each end (a broken end has neither). Diameters 1.0–1.9 c

Cross-section profile layer: each tube is stroked into a canvas as concentric bands of the cylinder height `h = sqrt(1 - r²)` with a material code (clear, coated, black paint, metal). The shader takes the normal from a Sobel gradient of that profile: gas colum
Emission layer at half resolution, blurred into a pyramid, used twice: as light on surfaces (lobes sized in metres, 2 cm to 3 m) and as bloom on screen. Bricks and tiles get relief toward the light.

Characters from silhouettes. Build each pose from a small rig (haunch, body, chest, neck, head, muzzle, ears, two-segment legs) as a smooth union of signed-distance shapes; take the outer contour with marching squares, smooth it and open it at one point for th

Hanzi from the font's skeleton. Lay each character on a 10 × 10 grid over the skeleton of a sans-serif CJK font (Noto Sans SC): horizontals level, verticals plumb, strokes joined into as few bent tubes as the shape allows, double-backs routed behind lit stroke

The street is procedural and anchored to the world: brick, mosaic tile, plaster, shopfronts with dim interiors, roller shutters, AC units, drainpipes, cables; a dark alley is a near-black slot between buildings.
colour_logic: The ground is dark and neutral (night facade, wet asphalt); hue comes only from tubes and the light they cast.
Gas colours follow the physics above. Give each sign its own hue so the street reads as a sequence.

Characters own their hues: a hero hue for the protagonist and a contrasting one for whoever it meets (cool against warm reads best); no sign in the same shot uses either. A character keeps its hue wherever it goes.
Values: tube core > halo > lit wall > unlit wall > sky. Nothing painted may be brighter than a lit tube.
motion: 30 fps; every switch lands on the music grid (beats, 8ths, 16ths).

Strike: 100 % for 50 ms, dark 70 ms, 70 %, dark, ramp to full in 0.1 s. Argon-mercury tubes start dim violet and warm to blue. A figure can also come alive by light running along its tube from one electrode to the other.

Characters switch, they never tween. One key pose per beat or per 8th note; pose changes are instant. Make poses strong: a leap stretches into one line, a landing gathers into a ball; a gallop alternates gathered and extended frames. Afterglow, if any, only on

Failure: random flicker; a crack flashes white at the impact and leaves a visible gap in the tube; the column turns pale; the glow retreats a section at a time toward the electrodes. Anything stacked (water levels, steps, a meter) dies a level at a time.
Chasers and alternate circuits: arrows and borders fill in 16ths; two outlines of one object in different gases swap on the beat.
A slight mains shimmer (±3 %) on everything lit; rain falls at 6–8 m/s; ripples die within a second.
camera_grammar: Macro on cold glass or an eye, pulling back
Lateral truck with a hanging sign in front
Crane down to puddle level (eye 0.3 m)
Rise from the reflection to the sign
Pull back and rise to the whole street
Tilt down into a still puddle
sound_palette: The medium's own sounds: transformer hum at 100/120 Hz with buzzy harmonics, the click of each flash, relay clacks for chasers and switched frames, crackle for a failing tube, a glass ting and sizzle for a crack, rain on wet asphalt, drips, the plop of a drop
Characters speak in neon: a creature's breath is the hum with a tremor, footsteps are relay clicks, a landing is a soft thump; no animal voices.
Water inside a sign: a falling gurgle for draining, a drip on dry glass, a splash.

Music: synthesised city pop / electronic pop at a dance tempo; each sign that strikes plays the next note of a rising line; signs going off play a falling one. Silence is hum: when the music stops, the transformers are left.
pitfalls_limits: Flat glowing strokes look like vector art: always render the cross-section and the board behind.
Wrong gas colours (a green clear tube, a blue neon): only neon and argon-mercury may be clear.
Hand-guessed hanzi: strokes in the wrong place, double-backs crossing the character, one tube per stroke with caps everywhere. Lay them over the font.
Tweened or morphing figures break the medium; so do bright, long afterglows that multiply a character.
Macro bloom: very close to a lit figure the halo floods the frame; pull back a little or keep most of it unlit.
Low cameras need off-screen content: a mirror at puddle level shows signs far above the frame; keep them in the layers or frame higher.
A small figure in a wide shot (≈ 100 px) reads as a streak; use wides for the street's answer, mediums for the character.
Readable text vs flashing: let a sign settle before it chases.
styles.engine_section: - `demo/lib.js`: `fillet`, `tubeFromStrokes(strokes, {D, z, coat, col, circ, caps})`, `hanzi`, `latin`, `track`. - `demo/world.js`: gas colours `GAS`, the street (signs, boards, shopfronts, buildings), `artTube` (a tube from rig output, scaled, flipped, placed). - `demo/film.js`: `drawTube` (profile + colour + emission, partial lighting), `strike()` and `circuit()` (switching), character keys (`K_`, `jump`, `run`), the cracked tube, cameras per shot, `window.TEXTS`, `window.EV`. - `demo/gl.js`: surfaces and glass shading, wet street, puddles, ripples, post. - `demo/tools/art.py` + `sdf.py`: th

styles.name: Caption News
styles.official_demo_line: America lost 1.3 million bee colonies, yet the count rose 6 %: a news short that works with the sound off.
styles.principles: 1. Sound-off first. Every beat must be understood from the picture and the captions alone; the voice adds pace, not information. 2. The caption is the shot. One Chinese line, set huge, slammed in two or three chunks, one keyword in a yellow block; one English line under it. The footage is chosen to sit under the line. 3. Evidence on screen. Each number arrives with its source: a source tag slides in; key figures are first seen highlighted in the original document; per-shot footage credits sit in the corner like a news "Video:" tag. 4. A hook on frame 4. The film's largest number lands in the f
colour_logic: Cuts on a 120 BPM half-beat grid (every cut at a multiple of 0.5 s). Footage shots 1.5–3 s; data cards and documents 3–4.5 s; a shot that holds a comparison stays until every item has been fully on screen ≥ 2.5 s.

Captions cross cuts. A caption can run over two shots (picture changes, words don't); captions change at most every ~2.5 s even when shots change every 1.5 s. Reading time, not shot length, sets the caption clock.
The order of a fact: footage (feeling) → the number on a card → the document line that says it → the consequence. Never a number without its source tag in the same shot.

Transitions are few and fixed: hard cut (default); a 1–2-frame white flash on the turn and on the freeze; a card sliding in from the right with speed streaks (0.18 s); a split screen opening from its divider; grid panels rising staggered (0.1 s apart); a punch
motion: Ledger card (the data-card ground): `#151512` sheet, faint ruled lines every 54 px (4.5 % white), a thin red double margin at x 78/86 — the "account book" that ties every chart together. It slides in from the right over 0.18 s; inside, a slow push (×1.025–1.03

Colour meaning: honey `#FFC21A` = the point / gains / the highlight; red `#FF4A3D` = losses, the spike, the bad number; ivory = everything else; grey `#8D8B83` = labels and units; `#5E5C55` = the bars that don't matter.

Numbers: Inter Tight 800 with fixed-width digit cells (`num()` in `demo/main.js`), so a rolling counter never jitters. Counters roll with ease-out and turn their colour when they arrive. Units in Chinese (箱, 万箱) set smaller after the number.

Charts: titled top left in Chinese (Noto Sans SC 900 64 px, ≤ 6 characters so it can be read in the shot) with one grey English line; lines draw segment by segment (eio); the key point gets a bigger dot, an expanding ring (0.7 s) and a block label; bars grow f

Map: state shapes from Natural Earth (maps follow DIRECTOR.md §13), projected (Albers), sequential fill in five steps of one hue, states without data in dark grey with a "未单列" legend swatch; the subject state outlined in yellow with a leader and a label; the m

Documents: the PDF page rendered at 220 dpi as white paper on a dark desk (±1–2° tilt, soft shadow, vignette), pushed in slowly; highlighter rectangles placed from `pdftotext -bbox` coordinates (1 pt = 3.0556 px), `multiply` blend, swept left → right in 0.3–0.
pitfalls_limits: Wikimedia Commons (video and photos): read the licence on each file page. Fine: CC0, public domain, CC BY (credit author, title, licence on screen and in `CREDITS`). Not used: CC BY-SA, "no known restrictions", unclear licences, YouTube re-uploads, colourised

U.S. federal agencies (USDA, USGS, NASA, NOAA, NARA): works of federal employees are public domain; check that the page does not credit a contractor or a third party. NASA: https://images.nasa.gov. NARA: https://catalog.archives.gov.
Internet Archive: only items whose own page states public domain or a CC0/CC BY licence; U.S. works published before 1931 are public domain.
Library of Congress: read each item's rights statement; "no known restrictions" is not enough.

Official documents and data (reports, statistics, court filings) from the agency's own site: the source of every fact; keep `FACTS.md` (claim, URL, quoted wording, derived sums with their arithmetic).
Map geometry: Natural Earth (public domain). Its default borders are not usable for China: DIRECTOR.md §13.
styles.engine_section: Copy `demo/` into the project and replace the content: - `main.js` — the page (`window.render(t)` draws synchronously with placeholders first, so `TEXTS(t)` is valid for `readcheck.mjs`, then loads the frames it needs and draws again). Shot functions per format; `SHOTS` table for cuts. - `timeline.json` — captions (`zh` with `|` chunks and `{keyword}`, `en`), voice start times, silences and hits; read by the page, `tools/cues.py` (.srt + timing check) and `audio/mix.py`. - `tools/prep.sh` — every video shot as a 30 fps JPEG sequence at its display size (crop, lanczos, unsharp, delogo); report

styles.name: 1920s Newsreel
styles.official_demo_line: 1926: the papers say the Charleston will ruin America's knees; at Ford's own picnic the kids dance it anyway.
styles.principles: An edit style: the look is in how real material is arranged, cut, captioned and carried by sound, not in a drawing technique. - Archive in a projected gate: 1.37:1 picture, full height, rounded corners, black outside; everything inside it shares one silver grade, gate weave, flicker, scratches and dust. - News objects do the explaining: newspapers, magazine pages, books, telegrams, maps, records. They are filmed (spun, slammed, panned, turned, underlined), never typeset as slides. - A voice talks over everything: short exclamations, half joking, never a lecture. - Music is a band, and it edits
construction: Gate: 1480 × 1080 inside 1920 × 1080 (1.37:1), corner radius 26 px, pure black outside. Nothing is ever drawn outside the gate.

Two layers: the picture layer (footage, print, maps, cards) gets the film look; the type layer (place cards, labels, subtitles, the record inset) stays sharp and steady. Grease-pencil marks belong to the picture (they weave with it).

Base grade for every source, before anything else (`tools/prep.py`, `grade()`): greyscale → percentile stretch (0.6 % → black, 99.6 % → white; print: 0.2–0.3 % / 99.0–99.7 % with the black lifted to 26–30, like newsprint) → mild S-curve `x + 0.18·(x−0.5)·(1−|2

Projection look (`filmLook()`, picture layer only): warm silver (`multiply #efe7d6`, `screen #17140f`), vignette 0.42 H → 0.95 H, flicker ±3.5 % per frame + 3 Hz drift, gate weave ±1.6 px / ±2.2 px (value noise), 0–3 vertical scratches that live for 9 frames,

Archive film upscaling: at most ~2.5×. NTSC transfers (720 × 480) are treated as 4:3, cropped to 1.37 and scaled 2.31× to 1480 × 1080: `hqdn3d=4:3:6:5` → `lanczos` → `unsharp=5:5:0.55` → base grade. Frames are exported at 24 fps as JPEG sequences and played by
Print: newspapers, magazines and books at their scan resolution; crop pages to the relevant fold so unrelated (and sometimes ugly) old stories never come into view.
colour_logic: Monochrome warm silver for the picture; values do the work (check every shot as a thumbnail).
Type is cream on near-black (`#f3eee4` / `#d6cfc0` on `rgba(12,11,10,.8)`), framed by a 2 px cream rule; marks are a slightly warm white grease pencil; underlines on printed pages are dark soft lead.
Packaging silver: Art Deco gradient lettering `#fff → #d9d4ca | #9e978a → #efebe2` with a hard "metal" break at the middle and a black outline (0.12 em).
No colour accents, no sepia wash on top of the silver, no colourised archive.
motion: The band is the clock: pick a hot-dance tempo (190–220 BPM); every cut, landing, slam and label entrance sits on a beat, most cuts on bar lines; quick inserts on beat 3 or on the Charleston accent (beat 1 and the "and" of 2). When a period record plays, cut on
One story = one place + one kind of material + one line of voice. Stories get shorter towards the end (2–3 bars → 1 bar → beats), then one held button.

Shot lengths: archive shots 1–2.5 s; print and documents 2.5–4 s (they must be read); comparisons ≥ 2.5 s fully in frame before the verdict; never a static frame longer than ~1 s without something moving (push, roll, pencil, flicker of a counter).

Transitions are the newsreel's own, each used once, as punctuation: iris close/open, diagonal hard wipe with a bright 6 px edge, vertical-axis flip, venetian blinds (12 slats turning), clock wipe from 12 o'clock, spinning paper, page turn, panel push-over, fre
L-cuts: the announcer may run 0.3–0.5 s over a cut; a new music state may start one beat before its picture (J-cut).
camera_grammar: Slow push then punch-in on a beat
sound_palette: Announcer (Kokoro): a bright, energetic male voice; a blend of two voices (e.g. `am_liam:0.6,bm_george:0.4`) gives a mid-Atlantic tinge; speed ≈ 1.15–1.2; 6–12 words per line, exclamations and rhetorical questions. Treatment as a 1930 optical track (`period_vo

Band (original): tuba on 1 and 3, banjo four to the bar (accent 2 and 4), trombones on the Charleston figure (1 and the "and" of 2), snare backbeat, honky-tonk piano right hand, muted then open trumpet melody with clarinet a sixth below, woodblock pickups; a b

Counter-music: when the story has two sides, give the other side its own band (here an old-time reel: fiddle, plucked dulcimer, upright piano, tuba) and let them trade bars, then half bars, in a split screen, panned left and right.

Archive record: a public-domain 78 can take over the soundtrack as "the real thing": needle drop (click + surface noise), band-pass 110–6500 Hz, crackle and rotation rumble only while the needle is down, varispeed by ≤ 2 % to sit on the film's tempo; end it on
pitfalls_limits: U.S. National Archives (films, often via Internet Archive "FedFlix" copies): federal works are public domain; donated collections need their own rights note (e.g. the Ford Motor Company Film Collection: all rights transferred to NARA in 1962, "copyright- and r
Internet Archive: check every item's licence field and provenance; skip anything that is a YouTube mirror, a colourised or "restored/AI enhanced" version, or has no stated source.

Wikimedia Commons: read the licence template on the file page; use PD-US-expired, PD-US-no-notice, PD-USGov, CC0, CC BY. A Library of Congress "No known restrictions" (often with "Copyright-tag-still-required") is not enough, nor is DPLA "no known restrictions
Library of Congress (loc.gov, tile.loc.gov; Chronicling America newspapers before 1931), NASA, other national archives.
Print: anything published in the US before 1931 (newspapers, magazines, books on archive.org / HathiTrust / Commons) is public domain in the US.

Recordings: US sound recordings published before 1926 are public domain in the US from 1 January 2026 (Music Modernization Act: 100 years after publication for pre-1947 recordings); UCSB Library / Internet Archive transfers (Edison, Victor) and the LOC Nationa
Maps: Natural Earth (public domain) for outlines drawn in code. Its default borders are not usable for China: DIRECTOR.md §13.
styles.engine_section: - Catalogue descriptions matter: a picnic film can contain both old-time dances and the Charleston; use only the shots that match the claim. - Archive transfers start and end with archive slates, "End of Recording" and white flashes; cut inside them. Remove watermarks and archive logos. - Newspaper pages hold unrelated, sometimes offensive stories next to yours: crop to the fold you need. - Per-frame auto-levels make footage pump; use one level set per clip. - `destination-in` irises leave transparent corners that later turn grey under `screen` — paint black behind with `destination-over`. - C

styles.name: Live Countdown Split-screen
styles.official_demo_line: The last minute of the Artemis II launch, uncut: one cell opens to nine, and they merge into one at ignition.
styles.principles: 1. Real time. One continuous stretch of the event, never cut, never re-ordered, never sped up. Slow-motion sources are played back at real speed. The clock and the picture can be checked against each other at any frame. 2. The clock is the lead. It ticks every whole second (sound and a falling digit), it says who is in control, and it changes state at zero. 3. Cells show the same second. Every video cell is synced to the clock, or says plainly that it is not (§8, "sync badge"). 4. The layout is the edit. Cuts are layout changes, and every layout change lands on a real spoken call or event in t
construction: Three kinds of material at once: video cameras of the same moment (2–8), documents (a fact sheet, a filing, a schedule: shown as paper, never retyped as a slide), and photographs (the people of the day). Our own type explains them; type printed in the material
Data drawn by us: checklists, bars, a flight or process profile, a second countdown to the next milestone. Every number comes from an official source (§10).

Cells: hard rectangles on near-black `#06080A`, 24 px outer margin, 8–9 px gutters, 1 px border `rgba(222,232,238,.16)`, a light radial vignette (to 36 % black) on video cells. No rounded corners, no drop shadows, no 3D.
Camera chip top-left of every cell: dark plate 84 %, a square dot (orange = synced video, grey = unsynced or still), code (`CAM 4`, `DOC`, `LIST`), Chinese name, small English name.

Burned-in text in the sources (broadcast bugs, camera IDs, timers, tracker readouts) is cropped by a per-shot usable region, or blurred out (ffmpeg `delogo`) after it has been used for syncing. Never shown as if it were ours.

One grade for every source (ffmpeg): `eq=contrast=1.07:saturation=0.9:gamma=0.97:brightness=-0.01,colorbalance=rs=-0.02:bs=0.03:rh=0.03:bh=-0.02`, then film grain 1 at the master (`mux.sh … 1`). Cool shadows, slightly warm highlights: control rooms and launch
motion: 30 fps. Clock: on each whole second the new digits drop 14 px in 0.12 s (ease-out); the sub-second bar empties one segment per 0.1 s (fills after zero).

Re-layout: 0.34 s `easeInOutCubic`. Cells that stay interpolate their rectangles; new cells open from their left edge; leaving cells close to the left; a new cell flashes a 3 px orange border for ~0.2 s when it lands. A grid filling up pops one cell per spoken
Swaps (one source replaces another in the same rectangle) wipe in from the left. Hard cuts only between full-screen sources.
Photographs push in ≤ 6 % over their whole stay; names pop one by one 0.16 s apart. Documents move their window down a row in 0.45 s; the highlight sweeps left to right in 0.35 s.
Never: slow push-ins on video to fake motion, page-turn transitions, centred pop-up words, speed ramps.
sound_palette: Mix: music about 8–10 dB under the native sound and ducked under speech; the ignition (or the event's own climax sound) is the loudest moment; master −14 LUFS via a pre-limited mix so `mux.sh` meets the true-peak target.

Changing the music (e.g. a Suno track): never move the clock or the cuts; choose or stretch a track so a downbeat lands exactly on zero and a section change lands on T−10, and keep the quarter-second silence before zero.
native_moves: The grid fills on the count.
pitfalls_limits: Unsyncable footage (an edited "rover" reel with no clock or event to align on). Never fake it: label the cell "same window · not frame-synced", keep it out of the countdown's key seconds or use it only where nothing it shows contradicts the time, and say so in

Measuring zero. Never trust metadata. Combine two independent marks: a visible event (ignition flash, a broadcast countdown bug's flip) and the spoken word timing ("booster" at zero). Re-measure on the file you actually cut: `ffmpeg -ss … -c copy` starts on th
Audio and picture of one file can disagree (a switched feed whose audio lagged its video by ~1 s). Sync each camera on its picture.
Slow-motion sources: measure the factor from two events with a known gap (e.g. engine start to booster ignition = 6.36 s) and re-time with `setpts=PTS/k`.

Burned-in text: broadcast bugs, camera numbers, timers, tracker data. Define per-shot usable regions (they change when the source cuts) or `delogo` them; check every source cut with a frame-difference scan.
A static wide shot for ten seconds reads as flat. Give every 1–2 seconds a new element (a cell, a tick on the list, a flag, a punch-in), not a fake camera move.
Spoilers in the subtitle: a whole-sentence Chinese line reveals the end of a count early. Split counts into separate cues.
The clock jitters if digits are proportional: draw them in fixed slots.
styles.engine_section: Materials — ask first. Before searching, ask the user whether they have their own material of the event: footage from several angles, recordings of the audio, photos, documents (schedules, filings, results), data. What they give comes first and is credited as they say.

styles.name: City Symphony
styles.official_demo_line: One day in New York in time-lapse: rivers of light, a grid on the sixteenths, 1899 beside today.
styles.principles: - An edit style. The picture is real footage of a place (time-lapse, hyperlapse, aerials, slow motion, archive film, photographs). The style lives in *how time is bent* and *where the cuts fall*, not in a drawn look. - The score is the script. It is written first, with a clear arc: minimal repetition → acceleration → climax → a sudden stop → acceleration again → hard stop → a quiet coda. Every cut sits on a beat or a subdivision of it. - Machines fast, people slow. Cars, trains, clouds and light are sped up until they become lines; the one slowed moment is something fragile (a soap bubble, ste
construction: Footage only (2D). Sources mixed freely: tripod time-lapse, long single-camera time-lapse (≥ 12 h, sunrise and sunset in the same frame), hyperlapse, drone aerials (top-down is gold), high-frame-rate slow motion, archive film (pre-1931), photographs (a pair fr

Everything is unified into one 35 mm release-print look: 1.85:1 matte (21 px bars on 1920×1080), warm highlights, lifted blacks, highlight bloom, clumped mid-tone grain, ±0.5 px gate weave, soft vignette.
Never generated images; never restored, colourised or speed-corrected archive copies; never YouTube mirrors of archive films.
Upscale limits: archive ≤ 2.5× (denoise → lanczos → light sharpen → grain); modern ≤ 1.5×.
motion: Speed is the main instrument. Shot speeds run from 0.3× to 75×; every speed above 1× uses frame blending (a 360° shutter): each output frame averages the source frames it covers, capped at N frames. Headlights become continuous lines, crowds become fog, clouds

Speed ramps are smooth (smoothstep between key speeds) and always mean something: a corridor accelerates out of real time (1× → 6×), a time-lapse ramps into a frenzy (1× → 7×), a fast shot brakes into slow motion (2.2× → 0.3× in 0.55 s) on the bar where the mu

Camera moves are added sparingly in post: slow push-ins (1.00 → 1.05–1.10 over the shot), a falling push on the opening still (1.0 → 1.3 in 0.35 s, ease-out, then accelerating to ×2 by the cut). No shakes, no whip pans, no digital zooms past the upscale limit.
camera_grammar: Dry cut of the whole ensemble, reverb left ringing
sound_palette: Music only. No narrator, no source sound (the footage soundtracks are other people's music), no sound effects. A narrator would turn watching into listening and would fight the score for the structure; that is why the style has none. If a voice is ever require

Orchestration (sampled, CC0 — `core/audio/sampler.py`): pipe organ (full and soft stops, pedal), winds staccato (flute, clarinet), strings (spiccato cellos and violins, sustained cellos, violins, double bass), horn pair for the last two bars, concert bass drum

Writing: arpeggios over a one-chord-per-bar progression; additive layering (eighths → triplets over eighths → sixteenths); the *break* is all arpeggios stopping at once into one held chord (maj7 or 9th); the return is a full-organ hit; the hard stop is a dry c
Reverb: `S.room(size .7, mix .28)` for the body, `size .78, mix .36` for the coda. Master to −14 LUFS / true peak ≤ −1 dBTP with `core/render/mux.sh` (grain 0: the grain is already in the picture).
pitfalls_limits: Watermarks and slates hidden in CC footage: corner logos (scale from the centre until they leave frame, within 1.5×), opening thank-you cards, end-card music credits, title text over the first shots. Check a 1-second contact sheet (`tools/secsheet.py`) of ever

Hidden cuts inside sources. Hyperlapse reels hide 2–3-frame jump cuts and whip transitions; frame blending across a cut makes ghosts. Scan with `ffmpeg … select='gt(scene,0.25)',showinfo` and keep every clip's source window inside one shot.
Too much blending turns noon clouds into grey mush: about 40 % shutter (24 of 60 frames) looks better than 100 %.
Grey-world balance kills night: it washes sodium light to white. Strength 0 for night shots.
Tracking needs a fixed camera. A drifting drone flags every building as motion. Use a median background only on tripod shots; for moving aerials use blending instead.
Motion-compensated slow motion tears thin lines (cables, rails, text): use the crossfade mode there.
Text over bright sky disappears: put number cards over the dark half of the frame or add the soft darkening; never a box.

A slow face is not a free subject. Do not make an identifiable ordinary person the slowed or close-up hero. Slow a thing; show people as crowds, tracks or ghosts. Public figures and people in news events are a different case.
styles.engine_section: 1. Ask the user first whether they have their own footage, photographs, documents or data for the place: their own time-lapses, a phone hyperlapse, family photos, a city's open data. Their material comes first. 2. If not, search these sources (all searchable with `demo/tools/footage.py`, which records title, author, licence and page in `SOURCES.jsonl` and writes `SOURCES.md`): - Wikimedia Commons — modern time-lapse, aerial and slow-motion footage under CC BY / CC0, photographs (for example the Carol M. Highsmith Archive, dedicated to the public domain), scans of old maps and books. Check the

styles.name: Visual Investigation
styles.official_demo_line: Newsreel, photos, testimony and the 1937 inquiry on one clock: five sources point to the same spot.
styles.principles: 1. Sources meet at one moment. The payoff of every section is two or more independent sources (a frame, a photo, a testimony, a report line, a sound) pointing at the same place or the same second. Cut points are sync points. 2. One clock, read in the picture. Time is carried by large readouts that belong to the layout: the timestamp on each telegram card, a playhead with its clock on the data chart, a `T+xx.x` stopwatch over the decisive seconds, a frozen "32 s". The scale changes with the story (hours → minutes → seconds → days) at section cuts. A permanent timeline band under every shot is o
construction: Three kinds of source at least: moving image (newsreel, CCTV, phone video, launch camera), documents (testimony, memo, telegram/teletype, report page), photographs. Add sound (original commentary, radio, recordings), data (weather, telemetry, counts) and maps

Documents: a scanned page is shown as a strip or a page, never re-drawn; only the decisive line is highlighted (red, `multiply`, α ≈ 0.6, wiped left to right). Text that exists only as a transcription (a report, radiograms) is re-typeset by code and labelled a

Archival picture pipeline (pre-1950 film, max ≈ 2.5×): deinterlace (`bwdif=0`) → crop borders → deblock (`hqdn3d=2:2:3:3`) → lanczos upscale → light unsharp (`5:5:0.5`) → greyscale; one grain for everything. Modern footage: ≤ 1.5×. Never colourised or "restore

One grade (canvas `ctx.filter`): footage and photos `grayscale(1) contrast(1.22) brightness(0.94)`; paper `grayscale(1) contrast(1.05) brightness(0.86)` (white pages pressed to light grey); maps greyscale, inverted, `brightness(.62)` so they read as dark line
One grain: six 256² Gaussian tiles rotated per frame, `overlay`, α 0.22 on footage/photos, 0.10 on paper. Grain only on sources, never on type or lines (`mux.sh … 0`).
Drawn evidence (plan, side schematic, charts, dot matrix) is thin line work on the panel colour, marked *schematic* when it is not measured.
motion: 30 fps. Elements cut in (≤ 0.1 s opacity) with a 3–4-frame white flash, as if pulled from the evidence locker; nothing flies, bounces or scale-pops.
Only things that are *drawn* are progressive: circles drawn clockwise in 0.5 s (ease-out cubic), leaders and links 0.4–0.8 s, plans stroke by stroke, highlights wiped, typewriter text for telegrams.
Inside a frame: a slow push (≤ 1.9× on a map, ≤ 1.06× on a photo) is allowed; the "camera" itself never moves. Layouts change on cuts.
The event clock (chart playhead, stopwatch) eases between keyframes and moves at constant speed inside a timed run (each tick = one real second).
Scale changes (minutes → seconds → days) happen on section cuts, carried by the readout changing form (clock → `T+` stopwatch → date), not by a zooming band.
Something changes at least every second; holds are for verdicts only.
pitfalls_limits: Inference passed off as fact. Camera positions, photo times and offsets need `≈ / inferred / unlocated` on screen and in `FACTS.md`.
Early reports as facts. The first-night memo and the period newsreel often disagree with the final report; use them as images or as claims to check, never as the source of a number.
Faking a multi-camera event. With one licensable film, do not borrow clips of unclear origin; cross-check film + photos + documents + sound instead. The structure still holds.
Seams in "continuous" shots. An exposure jump or splice breaks timing; time durations from the official record and state the alignment error.
Time zones and clocks. Old reports may use standard time while the place ran on daylight time; pick one and state it once on screen (`18:25:00 EST` on the first readout).
Too much at once. One layout, one finding; at most five sources on a board, and the subtitle never repeats the heading word for word.

Too many words on screen. Keep only what this beat needs (main readout or heading, the highlighted original, one short tag per source). Eyebrows, English twins of every label, archive numbers, footnotes and translations the subtitle already gives turn the fram

Empty placeholder boxes for missing material. A grey "no footage" or "waiting for photo" panel looks like a render error. Fill the slot with real material, change the layout, or let the source appear when it starts.
styles.engine_section: 1. Ask the user first. Before searching: does the user have their own footage, photos, documents, recordings or data (dashcam files, a report PDF, a spreadsheet of readings)? Their own material always comes first. 2. Where to look, and how to judge the licence. Use `demo/tools/footage.py` (copy it into the project): `search archive|commons|nasa`, `files`, `fetch` (records licence, author and page into `SOURCES.jsonl`), `used`, `md` (writes `SOURCES.md`). - Internet Archive: the item's `licenseurl` and collection. The NARA-donated Universal Newsreels (1929–1967) are public domain; other newsree

styles.name: Constructivist Montage
styles.official_demo_line: The Empire State's 1931 brochure credits its builders; the site film and Hine's photos answer: 2,500 a day.
styles.principles: 1. Evidence, recut. Every picture is real material (archive film, photographs, documents) about the actual subject. The film's argument comes from how they are cut and set, not from illustration. 2. One printed sheet. All material is converted to the same two-tone print (warm ink → paper); red is the only colour and is laid on top as a printed element. 3. The beat is the editor. Cuts, slams, wipes and counts sit on a 120 BPM grid (or the score's tempo); sections accelerate by halving shot length. 4. Type is structure. Words and numbers are beams: on a −18° band, as solid blocks, stacked vertic
construction: Four kinds of element only: bands (red or ink, along the axis), windows (rectangles or parallelograms holding film or photographs), cut-outs (people scissored from photographs with a paper-white border), type blocks. Plus one paper-fibre texture over everythin

The print grade (one function for film, photos and documents): luminance → percentile stretch (film: one pair of percentiles per clip, so it never pumps; 0.7 / 99.5; photos 0.8 / 99.4) → S-curve `x + s·(x−0.5)·(1−|2x−1|)·2`, s = 0.32 (documents 0.18, they keep

Cut-outs: a person-segmentation model (u2net_human_seg via onnxruntime) → threshold 0.5 → median filter → largest component → 7 px paper border dilated outside the mask. The border is the medium's own look and hides the model's edge errors. Group photos rarely

Documents: scans at full resolution, never retyped. They are marked: a red highlighter bar in `multiply` over the exact sentence, a hand-drawn red ellipse round a heading, a red circle on a map. Drawings on a document (a chart, a map) may be lifted off the pag

Resolution ceiling: archive film ≤ 2.5× its source pixels on screen, modern footage ≤ 1.5×, photos ≥ 1 source px per screen px where possible. Prepare clips with `hqdn3d → lanczos → light unsharp` before grading; add grain only in the mux. A 720-line film tran
Paper fibre: a fixed seeded noise canvas multiplied over the frame at α 0.5; film grain 4 added by `mux.sh`.
colour_logic: Everything photographic is ink-on-paper; nothing else has colour. Red is never laid on red: a red block on a red ground becomes ink.
Alternate grounds to make cuts land: paper scene → ink scene → paper. In an acceleration the background itself alternates red / ink per cut.
motion: Grid: one tempo for picture and score (120 BPM: beat 0.5 s, bar 2 s). Every cut, slam, wipe and count lands on a beat, half-beat or sixteenth. The page exports these times as `window.EV`; the mix reads the same list.

Shot length: 0.5–2 s for footage; one idea per shot. A section may accelerate by halving: 0.5 → 0.25 → 0.125 s (never shorter than 3 frames). Holds are reserved for reading: a text block, a freeze, a comparison.
Cut rule: adjacent shots conflict in at least one of direction (left slam / right slam), value (paper / ink ground), or geometry (diagonal band / upright window). Never two paper documents in a row.

Nothing static for more than a second: inside a hold something moves (film in its window, a counter, a slow push, a frame-within-the-frame). Planned exceptions only: the comparison hold, one silence beat, the end card.
Transitions inside the medium (pick per cut, don't fade):
*red wipe*: a 260 px red band at 72° (perpendicular to the axis) sweeps the frame in 0.25 s, the next scene revealed behind it; it lands on the downbeat;
sound_palette: Score: an original machine ostinato (eighths, minor, e.g. D–D–F–D–A–D–E–F) in spiccato cellos + staccato bassoon, staccato tuba / trombone on the beat, snare sixteenth taps, xylophone for counts (one rising note per lit cell or built floor), horn / trumpet sta

Original sound alternates with music: in one section the orchestra stops and a real recording (a rivet gun, a machine, a crowd) carries the cut alone, each burst trimmed to its shot. Bring it in a beat early (J-cut).

Foley for every printed action: slam = low thump + steel clank; stamp = thump + clack; wipe and iris = whoosh; marker = filtered noise scrub; paper = band-passed rustle; floors and cells = pitched clanks.

Layers: ambience (a real site / street recording, about 20 dB under the voice, out for the silence), foley ducked 35 % under speech, music ducked 70 % under speech (≈ 10 dB under the voice), narration compressed and levelled by RMS. Master to −14 LUFS with the
pitfalls_limits: Internet Archive: read each item's `licenseurl` and description. Public Domain Mark / CC0 / CC BY are usable; *no licence field* is not. For a pre-1978 US film, check the title and end cards for a copyright notice: published 1930 or earlier = public domain in
Wikimedia Commons: read the file page's licence and its source institution. Public domain, CC0, CC BY (credit in full) are usable; CC BY-SA is not used in library demos.

US National Archives (NARA), Library of Congress, NASA, other US federal agencies: federal works are public domain; check each item's rights statement. "No known restrictions" (LOC, Flickr Commons) is not clear enough: name it to the user or find the same imag
Museums with open access (Met, Rijksmuseum, Smithsonian): CC0 where the object page says so; check that the item is still marked open access.
University and city libraries (e.g. Columbia's digitised ephemera on the Internet Archive): use their rights statement; "copyright status undetermined" is not usable.
styles.engine_section: Every number, date and claim on screen or in the voice comes from an official or primary source (a contemporary report, an official brochure, a government record), kept in `demo/FACTS.md` with the URL and the quoted wording. Counters are graphics: only their end values and dated anchors are facts. Where two primary sources disagree (a film's intertitle vs. the official brochure), use one and record the conflict.

styles.name: Sports Telestrator
styles.official_demo_line: Down 3–0 at half-time, Fenerbahçe scored three in 12 minutes: freeze, draw, split screen, shot map.
styles.principles: 1. Watch it, then take it apart. Every piece of action is seen moving before it is explained. A freeze always follows play; the explanation never comes first. 2. One freeze, one finding. Each freeze says one thing (the ball wasn't cleared; nobody stepped out; he struck it from outside the box) with one label and at most two groups of lines. The same few seconds of footage are reused, each pass going one layer deeper. 3. Drawn on the real picture. Rings sit under feet, arrows follow the ball's real path, the box line is traced over the real line. Nothing floats in an abstract diagram until the
construction: Full-frame footage most of the time. The packaging lives in the corners:

Corner bug, top right (x 1452–1880, y 38–110): show name on a yellow block + a mode line in the mode's colour — LIVE (red dot) / ANALYSIS (yellow) / REPLAY (cyan). It is in every footage frame from frame 1, because it sits over the broadcaster's logo.

Score bar, bottom right (x 1392–1880, y 926–996): HOME n – n AWAY + minute. The away number flips on the frame the ball crosses the line (a 0.5 s roll with a yellow flash). It sits over the broadcaster's URL.
Source clock, top left (x 40–370, y 38–90), on every analysis shot: `❚❚ 04.20s F106` — source seconds and frame number; ▶ ½ in slow motion, ◀◀ in a rewind. Hidden in live play.
Labels (black card, coloured left bar, Chinese line + small spaced English line) sit in empty grass or crowd, never over the action they describe.
Subtitle bar bottom, centred at x 880 (its right edge stays left of the score bar), y 938–1044.
colour_logic: Order inside one piece of action: live at 1× (original sound) → rewind (0.6 s, reversed with tracking bars and ◀◀) → freeze ① → slow play (0.6–0.85×, frame-blended) → freeze ② → slow play with a stopwatch → freeze ③ → ball flight with a comet trail → another a
Lighter variants for secondary pieces of action, so the deep breakdown stays special:
Freeze-in-play: no rewind; play at 1× up to the decisive pass, freeze, draw, then play on to the goal.
Dual-angle freeze: both angles play side by side and each arrives at the same instant (each at its own speed) where both freeze together; the same player is ringed in both.
motion: Labels: Noto Sans SC 900, 40 px (30 px for a name), English line Barlow Condensed 600, 21 px, letter-spacing 2 px, in the role colour.
Packaging numbers (score, minute, stopwatch, big data): Barlow Condensed 800 Italic.
Clock / frame numbers: IBM Plex Mono 500, 24 px.

Board pages: title Noto Sans SC 900 60–64 px, rows Noto Sans SC 700 34–42 px with a grey note under each, numbers Barlow Condensed 800 Italic 64–150 px in yellow; text appears left to right with a clip reveal.
No handwriting fonts anywhere: printed type on a dark card belongs to the same packaging; handwriting reads as a school notebook.

Subtitles: Chinese line (Noto Sans SC 500, 38 px) above an English line (Barlow Condensed 600, 32 px), black bar 0.64 with a 4 px yellow edge; one line per language, never wrapped — shorten the line instead of shrinking it.
sound_palette: Footage: `hqdn3d=1.2:1.2:2.5:2.5` → lanczos to 1920×1080 (modern footage at most 1.5×) → `unsharp=5:5:0.55` → `eq=saturation=0.9:contrast=1.04:gamma=0.97` + slightly cool shadows; one grade for every clip; film grain 2 added once at the master (`mux.sh`).
Broadcaster logos and URLs are covered by the packaging (bug and score bar placed exactly over them, present from frame 1), or kept outside split-screen windows — never by cropping past 1.5×.
Prefer a broadcaster's native resolution over an "AI-upscaled" stream.
styles.engine_section: 1. Ask the user first whether they have their own footage (club or academy video, their own camera, a licensed broadcast clip), line-ups, event data or photos, and the rights to use them. Their material comes first. 2. Where to look (judge every file on its own page): - Wikimedia Commons (search "goal", the match, the player): many clips are cut from broadcasters' own YouTube uploads under CC BY. Fine: CC0, public domain, CC BY. Not used: CC BY-SA, "no known restrictions", unclear licences. - A broadcaster's or club's own YouTube channel when its video page says *Creative Commons Attribution l

styles.name: Broadcast News Package
styles.official_demo_line: Four AI stories from one week in a full on-air package: rundown, headline strap, price board, spec card.
styles.principles: 1. One package system, used consistently. Every graphic is built from the same few parts: a brand plate (parallelogram), a tab in the accent colour, a paper strap, ink cards with an accent top edge, mono datelines, stamps. Viewers read the system before they read the words. 2. The bulletin's order. Sting → rundown ("today we have four stories") → item → item → … → back to the rundown, ticked off → sign-off. Each item opens with its category on the strap's tab and its date on the first graphic. 3. One fact per screen. A full-frame graphic states one thing: the price, the break, the two stocks,
motion: Chinese: Noto Sans SC 900 (headlines, strap) / 700 (labels).
Latin: Barlow Condensed 800 (numbers, names, the plate), 600 (secondary lines, quotes), 600 italic (the end-card English title).
Mono: IBM Plex Mono 500 for datelines, sources, axis labels, all caps with 1–4 px tracking.
All OFL, subset from Google Fonts by `demo/tools/fonts.sh` (the character list is read from `main.js`; delete `fonts/*.woff2` after a text change). No handwriting faces in this style.
Every label is bilingual on one line each (Chinese first, English smaller); never wrap.
sound_palette: 120 BPM grid, beat 0 at the end of the sting (1.5 s). Every cut and wipe on a beat or half-beat.
Shot lengths: sting 1.5 s; rundown 4–5 s; story shots 3–7 s; a map long take (6–12 s) as the bulletin's breath; a comparison stays until every item has been fully on screen ≥ 2.5 s.
A package action every 0.5–1 s inside a shot (flip, count, stamp, tick, strap change, map light, line step). No frame flat for more than 1 s; a strong action within 0.5 s of every cut.
Date every story: a weekly bulletin's items happen on different days; the date sits in the rundown row, the eyebrow line, the readout or the document.
styles.engine_section: 1. Facts first. Every on-screen number and every sentence of the voice comes from an official source (the company's own page, the exchange's data, the institution's press release or speech), recorded in `demo/FACTS.md` with claim, URL, quoted wording and any arithmetic. When a fact exists only in a news report, attribute it on screen and in the voice ("据…报道 / … reports") and keep to the plain claim; never put a single report's allegations about a real company or person on screen. 2. Data. Draw charts from real series only; when you have just a few reported numbers, draw a *schematic* line, tag

styles.name: Impasto Oil Painting
styles.official_demo_line: In a grey, rainy square one red umbrella opens, and a waltz paints the whole plaza in colour.
styles.principles: A moving oil painting made of knife strokes. Each stroke is a real object: a slanted plane of paint with a ridge where the blade pressed, a lip where it lifted off, broken streaks where the paint ran out, two colours dragged into each other. The world is repainted from its strokes every frame, but static paint never moves: only things that move in the story move. Light rakes across a height field, so the paint has body.
construction: Value first. Design each set as a flat, value-planned illustration (3 values minimum), then convert it to strokes. If the reference doesn't read at 480 px wide, no brushwork will save it.
Stroke sizes by importance and depth. Coarse to fine: large planes in sky and walls, a few px only at edges and faces (per shape: `maxR`, `detail`, `dir`).
Strokes never cross shape groups, so silhouettes stay crisp. Lost edges are opt-in (put two shapes in the same `group`).
Thin underpainting (the reference itself, blurred ~1.5 px) under the strokes, so the canvas never peeks through as outlines.

Knife stroke: longer than wide (≈ 1.7–3.1 × radius long, 0.95–1.45 × radius wide), slanted ends, small angle and value jitter (≈ ±13°, ±6 %). Solid objects that must read as silhouettes (figures, props) get little or no ragged run-out.
Light rakes over a height field; wet or glossy surfaces get slightly more specular.
colour_logic: Planes of mixed, slightly broken colour; each stroke may drag a second colour (`c2`) into the first. No gradients made by blending pixels: gradients are made by stroke-to-stroke steps.
Warm light against cool shadow is the default temperature structure; the brightest, purest chroma is reserved for the story's subject (a prop, a crowd, a light source), not the background.

Colour can be an event. Every stroke can hold a grey and a colour version; a monochrome world with one coloured exception, or a world re-laid from grey to colour, is native to the medium. The grey version is the luminance of the same strokes, slightly cool, wi

Examples of palettes that fit: an after-rain sunset (cobalt → peach → gold sky, ochre facades, full-chroma props); a harvest field (straw yellow, burnt sienna earth, one viridian tractor); a night kitchen (umber shadows, sodium-lamp orange, one cold blue windo
motion: Static paint is static. Only the things the story moves move (weather, figures, props, ribbons, light). Smooth 24 fps, no stepping: clarity is the brief.
Moving figures are procedural strokes rebuilt each frame from fixed seeds, so their paint doesn't boil (walk cycles, IK arms, props that open and close).
Actions sit on the music grid: a change of direction, a pop, a swell lands on a beat.
Anticipation → action → follow-through on every gesture (lift before the strike, dip before the snap, swing after the stop).
camera_grammar: Slow truck + push on a wide
Tilt-up from the ground or a reflection
Macro slide along the paint surface
Whip-pan into a new painted plate
sound_palette: Foley follows the paint and the world: palette-knife scrapes on every repaint or paint-over, wet dabs, the materials of the scene (wet stone, nylon, wood, fabric, glass).
Beds in layers (a hiss, near grains, one distinct detail), filtered when the camera goes under cover.

Acoustic instruments with a hand-made grain: solo strings, accordion, pizzicato, harp arpeggios, glockenspiel or celesta for pops, piano, guitar, woodwinds; a solo instrument for a lonely world, an ensemble for a shared one.

Options: one action = one sound = one cut (music-locked edit); pops pitched as a rising arpeggio so a sequence of events climbs; an unresolved phrase that the film resolves later; a hard silence that cuts music and beds to digital zero, containing at most one
pitfalls_limits: Confined strokes shrink near edges and leave canvas-coloured outlines → add the underpainting texture.
Draw order in the reference matters: painting the ground after the buildings covers their feet.
Plain rectangles read as posts or blocks → give silhouettes taper, a lit edge, and one or two defining dabs (shoulder, hair, handle).
Proportions carry the object's identity at this stroke size: a prop drawn too wide reads as a different thing. Check silhouettes at thumbnail size.
Film grain or heavy compression destroys the knife edges → no grain, supersample, high bitrate.
Strokes that are re-seeded every frame boil → fixed seeds per stroke.
Engine-level WebGL traps (reserved words, VAO binding) are listed in DEMO.md build notes.
styles.engine_section: Files: `demo/engine/impasto.js` (renderer), `demo/engine/plate.js` (reference → strokes).

styles.name: Urban Sketch · Pen & Wash
styles.official_demo_line: A park that is only a pen sketch; wherever the wind carries her straw hat, colour follows.
styles.principles: Reportage drawing, made on location in a few minutes. Two layers that stay visibly separate:
construction: Paper: two octaves of fbm mottling (a few %), a tooth tile multiplied over everything, figures included.

Ink: ~96 % coverage; world line width thinner far, thicker near (e.g. 1.3–3.4 px); wobble ~1 px; overshoot 3–8 px; a third to half of long strokes get one small gap. Strokes are baked with their draw time per pixel, so the shader plays back stroke order.
Wash: 2–3 rough-edged layers, multiply, alpha ~0.4–0.65, offset from the line by about one line width, a dried edge at 30–40 %; granulation = pigment × (0.82 + 0.36 · fbm).

Colour arrival field: every pixel has a time at which colour reaches it. The wash is revealed through it with a ragged wet front (darkened band just behind the front) and noisy edges. Figures bloom from a point with a noisy circular clip.
Foliage: pale base wash, then light and shadow masses, then small leaf dabs coloured by light direction, holes at the rim, scalloped ink only on the outline.
Sky: a few big soft washes at low alpha, fading upward; clouds are reserves with a tinted belly.
colour_logic: Ink is one colour (dark sepia or warm black); it never changes.
Wash is local colour, lightly: few pigments, mixed on the page; shadows are the local colour mixed toward one shared cool violet; distance mixes toward one haze.
Paper white is the brightest value; it is reserved, never painted.
Colour can be withheld: a page may be ink-only with colour as an event (one tinted object, colour arriving with a cause).
motion: Figures boil at 12 fps (line wobble and wash seeds change every 1/12 s). The static page does not boil (it is a real page); the camera moves every frame, smoothly.
Performance: anticipation, action, follow-through; footsteps on the beat.
Invisible forces are drawn: wind as ink curls that draw on and erase from the tail, trailing dabs; sound as ink lines; heat as wavy strokes.
Colour never snaps: it blooms from a point or arrives through the field.
Stroke-order draw-on for anything that "appears".
camera_grammar: Pull back to the whole page
Slow pan across a line-only area
