One light direction for the whole film (upper left by convention); heavier outlines away from it; tone fields come from the shape (pillow lighting, analytic spheres and cylinders), never from texture. Occlusion is geometric: lines stop at the shapes in front.

Roundels: double-ruled circle, ruled-machine ground with a white halo round the subject, content authored at a large radius and scaled in. Leaders: hairlines from a dot on the part to the rim, routed with clearance, a small italic figure number at the root.

Hand colouring multiplies over paper and under ink: a few px of spill, slight misregister, tide-line at the wet edge, low-frequency density lift, occasional backruns, granulation; each region blooms from where the brush touched.
colour_logic: The print is two values, paper and ink; all tone is line density.
Colour is transparent wash only, in muted earth and mineral pigments, one stronger pigment at most. Never opaque, never on lettering, rules or paper outside the figure.
Reserve it: the whole subject at one moment, or only the part that matters — or none.
Example wash sets: an amber insect with blue-grey wings; a map with a sea-green coastal band on buff land; one madder-rose organ on an otherwise black anatomy plate.
motion: Cutting order is the animation: outline → first hatching sweeping across each form → crossing → darks, hair, stipple. Strokes run at constant burin speed, many at once (a few for outlines, dozens for hatching).
A long single stroke may be followed by the camera; start it partly cut so no frame is empty. Keep a full build to a few seconds.
Roundels fly on an eased arc with a small lift, growing log-linearly to size. Colour blooms from one point with a ragged front and a wet rim that dries; regions staggered.
Nothing fades or slides like UI: lines are cut, text cut or written, colour blooms, sheets are pressed, peeled or laid down.
camera_grammar: Push to a part, ride with its roundel
Tilt/pan along the sheet at reading zoom
Locked frame, or a ≤ 2 % breathing push
Cut from mirrored copper to true proof
sound_palette: Foley by material: paper (peel crackle, slip tapped down, tissue rustle, sheet whoosh); press (roller rumble, thump); copper and steel (high band-passed burin hiss with chatter and faint plate ring, swarf pings, a tick on lift, circular scribe, burnishing rub)
Room: a quiet workroom (faint clock), paper room once the print exists.

Instruments (choose): harpsichord, string quartet, solo cello or viola da gamba, lute, chamber organ, glass harmonica for a cold subject. Plucked and dry while lines are cut; bowed or sustained only when something soft arrives; tiny tings for a scribed ring, a
Silence is real: cut room tone too, keep at most one small sound.
pitfalls_limits: Uniform width reads as pen → swell hatches, pinch contours between runs (`hatch({swell})`, `outline({run, pinch})`), keep wMin hair-fine.
Overlaps without occlusion → pass occluders as `excl` (subtracted ring by ring; even-odd would cancel overlaps).
Outline-only parts beside a hatched body → hatch along each part's axis, a dark at every joint.
Burin along the cut hides the groove; big skew looks like poking → ≤ 15°. Regular swarf helix reads as a spring → vary winding, twist, light one edge.
Reflections over grooves wash them out → copper light first. Roundels authored small freeze sub-pixel → author large, scale in. Leaders hugging the subject read as crossing it → clearance.
A long early stroke never draws → the ink's early exit must look ahead by the longest stroke.
A push-in cropping a fresh note breaks the reading rule → put consecutive details on one side.
Scientific names: TTS may manage, ASR won't → give the checker a plain spelling.
styles.engine_section: `demo/engine/`: `burin.js` (`B.Ink` ordered stroke store + `schedule`, `B.hatch`, `B.engraveTone`, `B.contourHatch`, `B.outline`/`B.stroke`, `B.stipple`, `B.fur`, tone fields), `plate.js` (`drawSheet`, `engraveText`, `writeScript`, `roundelFrame`), `wash.js` (`Wash`), `copper.js` (copper, burin, swarf), `index.js` (`engraveShape(svgPath, {at, light, spacing, style})`: any SVG shape → engraved figure). `demo/example/index.html` engraves and colours a four-pointed spark in ~20 lines; code and function table in DEMO.md "Engine reference".

styles.name: Silkscreen Travel Poster
styles.official_demo_line: A traveller crosses the world one full-bleed screen print at a time, a ticket stub counting the distance from home, until the far side turns into the way back.
styles.principles: A poster being printed on camera. Every colour is an opaque ink laid by its own pull; later ink covers earlier ink completely. No halftone, no fluorescent ink, no line work: a shape's edge is where one flat ink stops. Gradients are forbidden: skies and haze are stepped bands (a flat colour, thinning stripes, the next colour).
construction: One `Path2D` per ink layer, filled in the current transform's units; knock-outs are holes in the path. Any shape can be printed.
Pull reveal: a ragged squeegee front as a clip (a ~30 u drag tail); blade, bead and a sliver of handle ride on it.
Ink bead: a round tube with lit half, dark underside, rolling glints and viscous strands; a split fountain puts several colours in one bead.
Screen: a hinged frame with mesh, emulsion and tape; its shadow is a ring (even-odd), never a full rectangle.
Shapes: ridges with a jagged lit facet, pines as one outline of drooping tiers, water as a flat body with glint bars. Hard edges everywhere.

Poster templates: a portrait sheet (1000×1500 u: paper border, art area, a dark info band at the foot holding a name, a number, a rule and a row of stats; columns sized by content), or a full-bleed print (16:9, art to every edge, the name printed into the sky,
colour_logic: One palette per poster, ≤ 6 inks, assigned by role: light sky, deep sky / bands, far, mid, near (darkest; also the info band), and one bright accent (sun, route, highlights, key number). An optional lit-face ink.
Values step from far (light) to near (dark); depth is value, never blur.
The accent is rare: the sun or light source, the one route or product, the most important number.
Paper is a colour: an unprinted area is the brightest thing on the sheet (water, snow, a beam of light).
motion: Pulls are linear and steady (a squeegee does not ease). Accent inks start half a beat after the main ink of their layer.
Info items print left to right on subdivisions of the beat. There is no fade anywhere.
Screen lift: the frame hinges up (vertical squash + growing shadow) in ~0.4 s.
Palette re-ink: a wide squeegee travels diagonally over the sheet in ~0.35 s; geometry identical on both sides of the blade, only the inks change. Show only the blade, bead and a sliver of handle.
Loose layers: in a multi-plane move, planes parallax by depth with paper gaps and thickness shadows, then snap into register on one hit.
camera_grammar: Truck with the squeegee, slight roll, frame edge in view
Fast pull-back as the screen lifts
Push + tilt to the info band
Truck through a foreground silhouette (tree, lamp post, sail) in screen space
Slow lateral dolly along a row of prints
Push into the mesh until the weave shows
Log-zoom pull-back to the wall or window
sound_palette: Acoustic, hand-played instruments: strummed guitar, slide guitar, harmonica, upright bass, cajon or brushes, banjo, fiddle, accordion, harmonium, ukulele. Choose the family from the place: folk, surf, bossa or brass band all fit.
One pull, one hit: each ink lands on a musical event (a strum, a hit, a chord change); accelerate by subdividing, not by changing tempo. A registration snap is a loud downbeat.

Foley by material: squeegee on mesh (band-passed noise with a ~220–280 Hz mesh grain; faster = brighter), wet ink squelch, screen clack and hinge creak, paper stamps, ticks for dashed routes, paper hiss, a wood-and-metal clamp, drying-rack clips.
Ambience from inside the print: a finished scene may "wake up" (surf, street, crowd), J-cut in and L-cut out. Room tone under the table.
native_moves: The route as a printed layer.
pitfalls_limits: Stroke edge effects draw internal lines on unioned paths → fills only (fill, then fill shifted inside a clip).
A full-rectangle screen shadow muddies the print → ring shadow.
Cool shadow facets next to water read as water → shadows in the near ink.
Jagged ink beads read as paper edges → a round bead.
Parallax alone reads as "the mountains are moving" → paper gaps and thickness while loose, snapped to zero with a sound.
Silhouette wipes hold a dark blank → centre on the switch so full cover lasts ~1 frame.
Very wide banners are slivers in 16:9 → about 4:1.
Random coloured dots on the table read as confetti → a real workbench (planks, grain, muted stains, tape).
styles.engine_section: `demo/engine/silk.js` prints any shape in this style from a `Path2D`: `makeTextures`, `paperSheet`, `ink(ctx, {path, knock, paint}, {color, reg, clip, sheen, trap})`, `wipeRegion`/`wipeFront` (ragged pull), `squeegee` (blade, beads, split fountain), `screenFrame`, `inkFinish`, `bandSteps` (the gradient substitute), shape helpers. `demo/engine/poster.js` (full-bleed print with partial pulls and loose layers, ticket stub, end card, `pickInk` contrast), `demo/engine/scenes.js` (places as ink parts in print order, any print size), `demo/film.js` (timeline, cameras, sweeps). API table and a minimal

styles.name: Scratchboard Long Take
styles.official_demo_line: Red-crowned cranes in a Hokkaido valley, one scratchboard take, counted back from 33 to 1,927.
styles.principles: - Only ink, paper and one red. Every value is either ink or paper; grey exists only as a density of lines. One red is reserved for one small subject. A warm yellow may appear for the sun, a lamp or one material, never as a second accent. - Tone is cut, not shaded. Shadow sides of hills carry knife lines that run down the fall line; skies are parallel horizontal cuts whose width makes the light; snow is paper with a few drift strokes; water is ink with cut ripples. - Real depth, flat marks. The scene is built in 3D (terrain, rivers, thousands of trees, buildings), but every surface is drawn wit
construction: Render model: three.js scene at 2× supersampling, box-filtered down in a final print pass. Every material is a small shader that decides "ink or paper" per pixel; there is no lighting except one direction used to choose lit and shadow faces.

Two kinds of field. Every surface is either a paper field carrying ink cuts (lit faces, snow, sand, cloud, foam, steam) or an ink field carrying paper cuts (shadow faces, sky, water, forest, night). A cloud is paper with a few horizontal ink cuts on its unders

Faceted terrain: mountains and volcanoes are low-poly cones with flat facets. Lit facets are paper with a few fine ink cuts near the terminator; shadow facets are ink with paper cuts running down the slope. Cut spacing is fixed in world units so lines never sw

Sky in direction space: a sphere that travels with the camera; cuts are rows of constant elevation, so they stay horizontal and never slide with translation. Night = sparse wavy wind cuts and square stab stars; day = dense parallel cuts, thicker near the horiz

Billboard atlases drawn on canvas: trees (pines, frosted deciduous trees), animals, steam. Cylindrical billboards for anything standing, spherical with a screen rotation for anything flying. Sample the atlas with a negative mip bias and alpha-test so thin shap

Water is a ribbon cut into the snow (the ground is discarded inside a river mask), with bank walls and a paper snow lip. Ripples are short cuts across the flow, faded to solid ink where they would turn grey with distance.
colour_logic: Two values carry everything: ink (a warm black) and paper (a warm off-white). Never pure black or pure white, never a third grey fill.

One red, reserved for one subject, kept small (a crown, a lamp, a flag) and never smaller than about 3 px at 1080p; enlarge it a little rather than lose it. It may carry into the subject's own trace (its ripple, its trail), never onto another object. A flat st
A warm yellow is allowed for light itself (sun disc, its road on water, warm cuts in a dawn sky, a lamp) and one material at most. It never fills a large area except that one material.

Value order by depth: far mountains paper with ink shadow facets; forest bands solid ink; the middle ground paper; foreground ink silhouettes. Keep the subject on the opposite value of what lies behind it.
motion: Output 30 fps (`--fps 30` for `video.mjs` and `mux.sh`). The camera and the world move on every output frame. Separately, the print pass steps its paper flicker and blotches at 12 Hz inside the shader (`floor(t*12)/12`), whatever the output rate, so the image
Easing: long monotone curves; the camera keeps momentum through key positions and decelerates into every hold. No bounce, no shake except one frame for an impact.
Animals are flat silhouettes with three or four poses per action (sleep, wake, call, peck, walk, run, three wing frames, land, leap, bow). Wings cycle on fixed frames; never morph between poses.
Steam, snow and splashes are paper marks: horizontal cut wisps, square stabs, short arcs.
Mountains, horizon and sky texture never move; trees never sway.
camera_grammar: High wide establishing frame, sinking and pushing
Low glide over water or snow
Hold on a prop with words, long lens
Pass through a structure (bridge, gate, arch, tunnel)
Rise and pull back to the opening angle
Follow a flying or falling subject
sound_palette: Three layers. The world: the matter of the place (water under ice, frost cracking, wind in three weights, wings, steps on snow, small animal sounds). The print: knife through paper or wood, a block's thump, a sheet torn away, a seal pressed; used only on trans
Timbres that suit the medium: bowed vibraphone, harp, horn, low strings, pizzicato bass, xylophone, glockenspiel, timpani. Avoid synth pads and drum kits.
A three-beat or slow pulse that can stop; silence before a verdict, then one heavy low stroke.
A narrator, when there is one, sits on top: music ducks about 17 dB under speech and comes back up in the silent stretches; foley ducks about 7 dB.
native_moves: A plate of type in the sky.
pitfalls_limits: Close-ups expose the flat shading. 3D props pushed close to the lens look like toys. Keep living subjects to mid shot as flat silhouettes; give close props real materials (carved wood, concrete formwork, cast iron).
Empty paper. A field of snow without layers goes blank. Keep three layers in frame; add drift strokes, reed ticks, thickets, belts.
Grey sludge. Fine cuts at distance average to grey; fade them to solid ink or paper with distance and use negative mip bias for thin sprites.
Sliding lines. Any cut spaced in screen space swims as the camera moves; anchor cuts to world space (or direction space for the sky).
The road look. A dark river with a pale bank lip and regular dashes reads as asphalt. Break the rhythm of bank marks and keep the lip narrow.
Small subjects vanish. Real-scale animals disappear in a wide frame; draw distant ones up to 3× larger (a printmaker's scale), keep the red at its minimum size.

Camera through solids. Clear trees and posts from the camera path before placing scenery; check every low pass frame by frame. The same holds for every small scatter (reeds, stones, fence posts, grass): one within a metre or two of the lens fills the frame wit
Empty paper close up. A lit facet near the lens becomes a blank sheet. Make facets smaller near the camera path and give near lit faces their few ink cuts, grit or tufts.
styles.engine_section: The demo's code splits into a print kit any film can copy and the crane film's own world. Copy files into the project folder; nothing here is a library import.

styles.name: Pop Art
styles.official_demo_line: Almost every banana in the shops is one plant, copied: a wall of identical prints, an old banana eaten black by dots, and a wave of colour that turns into many bananas.
styles.principles: - A printed object, not an illustration. Four plates (red, yellow, blue, black key) on paper. Every middle tone is a dot screen; there are no gradients, no soft shadows, no transparency. - Dots live on the paper. The screen is fixed in page space at 45°: the closer the camera, the bigger the dots, until one dot is the size of a coin. Distance and emphasis are told by dot size. - Repetition is meaning. The same print pulled again and again, edge to edge, with small differences in register and ink: mass production, copies, sameness. Changing one tile's colourway against the wall is the strongest
construction: Three layers, one print pass (`demo/engine/pop.js`): a plates canvas whose R, G, B channels hold the density of the red, yellow and blue plates (1 = solid, 0.05–0.95 = dots, 0 = paper), a black key canvas (alpha), and a spot canvas for the rare unscreened colo

Opaque fills knock out what is beneath (plates, key and spot), so painter's order holds; `over` adds ink to what is already printed (red dots over yellow = orange shading, red and blue dots growing over anything = the print darkening).
Dot screen in page space, converted from screen pixels by the camera's inverse. Below about 2–4 px per cell on screen the dots fade into flat tint, so a wide shot never moirés.

Misregistration: each colour plate is offset from the key by a few page units (clamped to a few pixels on screen), so a white sliver shows beside the outline. Per copy, offset the fill from its key line by a different small amount: repeated prints are never id
Key lines are variable-width ribbons, heavier on the side away from the light (upper left), tapered at open ends; the line width compensates for local scale so small prints keep their outline.
Paper: warm off-white with light fibre and ink unevenness; age and roughness stay low (clean print). Raise them only to date a print (an older edition: more age, wider misregistration).
colour_logic: Three process colours plus black and paper. Every other colour is an overprint in dots: orange = yellow + red dots, green = yellow + blue, purple = red + blue, dark = red and blue growing over everything.
Primaries are used flat and big: one ground colour per poster, one subject colour, black for drawing, paper for breathing.
Never put a colour on itself (red type on a red ground, a yellow subject on a yellow ground without a key line or a paper disc between).
Darkness is never a black fill: it is dots of red and blue growing until the image drowns. Black is reserved for the key (lines, type outlines).
motion: Prints arrive in one of two ways: stamped (a short scale from 1.1 to 1 with the colour plates sliding into register, on the beat) or printed plate by plate (yellow, red, blue, black, each landing with a thunk).
Camera moves are long, eased, often logarithmic in zoom (a pull from dots to wall reads as one gesture).
Copies accelerate as they multiply: the interval between stamps shrinks.
Flips are card turns (scale X through zero), and the new print shows from the turn's midpoint.
Spreading things (a rot, a colour, a signal) move as a front with a gradient of dot sizes behind it.
Never moves: the dot screen relative to the paper; the paper itself.
camera_grammar: Pull from coin-sized dots to the whole print
Pull from one print to a wall of copies
Push into a round shape, match-cut to another round shape
Through a hole in a printed letter or number
Lateral track along a long print
Push to fill the frame with one tile, then flip it
Slow push into a wall while a front crosses it
sound_palette: The print shop is the foley: squeegee drags (band-passed noise), stamps (low thump plus a paper slap), paper whooshes for camera moves, a card flick for every flip, a single thunk per plate, a low granular crackle under anything that spreads.

Music in a sixties register: vibraphone, marimba, upright or jazz bass, conga, shaker, hand claps, muted and staccato trumpet; exotica, lounge or surf colours rather than orchestral pads. Darker passages strip the groove to a bass pedal and bowed vibraphone.
One-note-per-copy: a repeated visual event (each flip, each stamp) can carry a pitched note that climbs a scale.
Silence: before a turn, drop to a held low note for under a second; the first sound after it is a flip or a stamp.
pitfalls_limits: It turns into a comic. Panels, balloons and sound words make it a comic strip; keep labels as printed slips and give the story to the voice.
Dots in screen space. A screen-fixed dot pattern looks like a filter and swims under camera moves; always compute dots in page space.
Moiré in wide shots. Fade dots to flat tint below a few pixels per cell.
Dirty paper. Too much age, roughness or blotchy ink reads as a bad scan; keep it clean and use age only to date a print.
Same-colour collisions. Red on red, yellow on yellow: put a key line or a paper disc between.
Blank print moments. Printing plate by plate from an empty sheet leaves frames of bare paper; start with the first plate already down, and print a label's words together with its paper.
A key line that does not match its fill. When an image is made of tiles, the outline must follow the tile edges; a smooth curve over square cells looks drawn wrong, not misregistered.
Too many words. One label at a time, short Chinese lines, otherwise the reading-time rule cannot be met.
styles.engine_section: - `demo/engine/pop.js`: `createPop(canvas)` returns the printer. Drawing in page units: `begin(cam)`, `fill(shape, densities)`, `over(shape, densities)`, `black(shape)`, `line(shape, width, opts)`, `outline`, `ribbon(points, width)`, `text(str, x, y, {size, font, fill, outline, shadow, read})`, `measure`, `toScreen`; `present({cell, off, offMax, mask, age, rough})` prints the frame. `readBox` and `reads` collect readable text boxes for `window.TEXTS`. - `demo/banana.js` (the demo's subject; your film draws its own): `banana(pop, variety)` (curved body, stem, belly dots, highlight, ridge, misre

styles.name: Vintage Engraving Collage
styles.official_demo_line: A 1918 airmail sheet printed with its plane upside down: bought for $24, cut up and scattered, and number 66 is still missing.
styles.principles: - Real printed matter, cut by hand. Every figure is a cut-out of a real public-domain print (an engraving, a stamp, a news photo, a line drawing), with a slightly rough white paper margin around it. Nothing is drawn in a vector or 3D way to look printed. - Flat torn colour behind it. Large torn sheets of a few flat colours (teal sky, ochre disc, mustard sun, cream strips, paper clouds) make the space; their edges show a white fibre fringe. - It is paper on a table. Every piece has a thickness (a 1–1.5 px cut edge), a shadow from a top-left light that grows softer and further as the piece lifts
construction: Cut-outs: a scan, a hand-traced or computed mask, the scan's grey turned into ink amount on a cream card, a white margin dilated around the mask with a slightly torn edge. Line art with a transparent ground gets its silhouette by closing and filling holes. Han

Separated plates: a two-colour print (a poster, a label) is split into its ink plates by hue and re-inked in the palette; each plate can then be printed, shifted or turned on its own. Upscale before tightening the ink edge so lines stay crisp.
Torn colour papers: flat colour with a faint mottle, the edge displaced by fractal noise, a thin white fibre fringe outside it.
Old paper: a mottled cream base with fibres and faint foxing, lighter than a raw scan; it can be tiled with mirrored copies, so the table extends without seams.
Halftone: any photograph enters as a 45° dot-screen news clipping on newsprint, torn edges, a typed caption.

Paper physics in the composite: under each piece a cut-edge copy in a darker paper colour, offset down-right; two pre-blurred shadows mixed by height; the back side is paper colour with about 10 % of the mirrored ink showing through.
colour_logic: A restrained palette of six: old paper, cream card, warm black ink, ochre red, teal, mustard. Large areas are paper and flat colour; heavy black is limited to engraved lines, small slips and silhouettes.
A printed subject keeps its own inks, re-inked once into two tones close to the palette (for a two-colour poster: its red and its black), and only the subject uses them.
One colour carries meaning per film beyond decoration (ochre for the data wash and one key figure, mustard for the slip that names it); flat colour papers are scenery.
Example (our demo): paper #ECDFC2, card #F6EEDB, ink #221C17, ochre #C65F3A, teal #2F7F7A, mustard #E1AB3B; subject inks #C8463F and #2F5D8C; cut edge #B49D78, paper back #E9DFC8.
motion: On twos (12 drawings a second) for every paper piece; the camera moves smoothly every frame.
Slide in from off-frame with a small overshoot and a 2–3 drawing side-to-side settle; drops accelerate and bounce once; a slap arrives in two drawings (a slightly larger copy high above, then down).
Moving pieces carry a hand jitter (≈ 0.7 px, 0.25° per drawing); resting pieces are still.
Hinges turn around a pin and overshoot; a sheet can turn 180° flat on the table.
Flips around the vertical axis show the paper back and a wider cut edge mid-turn.
State changes are substitutions, not morphs: swap in a new cut-out (an open lid for a closed one, a printed sheet for a blank one).
sound_palette: Paper foley for every piece: slides (band-passed noise with fibre grain), pats when a piece lands, slaps for type, flutter for flips and wings, scissors snips, typewriter keys and the carriage bell, a rubbing roller, the scrape of a growing chart.

Score from small-ensemble period instruments: tuba and bassoon staccato, pizzicato strings, clarinet, xylophone, glockenspiel, harp, woodblock, timpani; a march or music-hall oom-pah, with a minor turn where the story turns. No generic piano and strings.
One near-silence before the turn, and transitions carried by sound (a whoosh through a shape, a whip).
With a voice: compress it and set it about 10 dB over the music; duck the music's 300 Hz–4 kHz band while it speaks.
pitfalls_limits: A cut-out without a margin or shadow reads as a digital sticker; one with a fat, even margin reads as a sticker too. Keep the margin thin and slightly torn.
Shadows from different light directions, or shadows that do not change with height, flatten the table.
Smooth scaling, fades and easing curves that never overshoot read as software, not paper.
Too many pieces: one subject per frame, about twenty flying pieces at most, leave the bottom-left free for subtitles.
Upscaled scans go soft and blotchy: separate and tighten the ink, use the largest public-domain scan, and keep cut-outs at or below their source size where possible.
Old-style serif figures in numbers, letters with outlines or glows, system fonts.
Copyrighted or "no known restrictions" images: only public domain and CC0 prints, each one in the credits.
styles.engine_section: - Python (numpy, scipy, Pillow) bakes the parts into `parts/*.png` and `parts/manifest.json`: paper and torn papers (`demo/src/bake.py`), cut-outs, separations, halftone, slips, subtitles, data engraving (`demo/src/bake2.py`, helpers in `demo/src/collage_lib.py`, the tone-to-line `engrave()` among them). - The page (`demo/index.html`, Canvas 2D) loads the sprites, derives each piece's cut edge, two shadows and paper back at load, and draws `render(t)`: keyframed poses on twos with overshoot, settle and jitter, scenes with their own cameras, transitions by clipping one scene inside a shape of a

styles.name: Swiss Motion Graphics
styles.official_demo_line: A concert poster lays itself out by five Swiss design rules; the fifth is to break just one.
styles.principles: - Pure 2D graphic design animated on a grid: flat paper, black type and bars, a very light grey and one saturated signal colour. - Every element snaps to the grid, every move lands on a beat, nothing bounces. - Rigor with one exception: the whole frame obeys a system, so the one element that doesn't becomes a character. - Extreme scale contrast: a giant numeral next to tiny technical notes.
construction: Frame grid: 1920×1080, 12 columns, ~96 px side margins, 24 px gutters, 24 px baseline. The frame can act as a spread: a left page (the programme: numeral, rule text, notes) and a right page (the artifact).

Artifact grid derived from the content (Gerstner): what the columns and rows *mean* is a design decision. Choose module sizes that give the elements mass; too many thin columns make a layout look like a chart.
Surfaces: page, paper, ink, signal colour, grid lines in two or three light greys (on page, while building, on paper). No gradients, no shadows, no particles, no grain (mux grain 0).
Bars and blocks are flat rects; consecutive cells of one unit merge into one bar, overdrawn 1 px at seams (antialiasing shows hairlines, especially when rotated or scaled).
A secondary voice can be light-grey elements under the black ones: depth without a second colour.
A 2D camera matrix (centre, scale, rotation) for all moves.
colour_logic: Paper, ink, greys, and one signal colour. Only one thing carries the signal colour; that makes it the protagonist. It is the only thing allowed to be inexact.
Overprint is allowed: black type on the signal colour.
The signal colour can be red, orange, ultramarine or green; choose it for the topic, then never add a second.
Examples: `#EAE9E5` page, `#FFFFFF` paper, `#111111` ink, signal `#E30613`; or `#F2F0EA` / `#141414` / signal `#FF5A00`; or `#E9ECEF` / `#0B0B0B` / signal `#1F3FFF`.
motion: Two curves only: a precise ease `cubic-bezier(.7,0,.2,1)` for snaps; linear for lines being drawn, playheads and the exception. No overshoot, no spring, no bounce.
Durations are note values at the film's tempo. A snap starts one note value early and lands on the beat.

Entrances are wipes or clip-reveals, never fades: words rise out of a clip rect from below the baseline and leave upward; lines grow along their length; paper appears by a wipe; big numerals climb in eased steps ("one module at a time").
Deletions are knife cuts: a thin line crosses the element, then the element collapses to its midline.
Ripples are ordered by distance from their cause, a couple of units per subdivision.
The exception moves differently: linear, unsnapped, perhaps pausing mid-flight; a coordinate readout beside it can turn from "on grid" to "off grid".
camera_grammar: Hard pan by one page or column
Pull out to a wall of artifacts
sound_palette: Music with a grid of its own: a steady pulse whose subdivisions give snap durations. Options: motorik / krautrock kit and bass, minimal techno, marimba or vibraphone patterns, a mechanical piano ostinato, a drum machine with a glockenspiel; one instrument adde
Picture and music can share one data file (a column → pitch, a row → onset), so a graphic can literally be the score.
Techniques (options): drop the drums for the one moment of the exception; a near-silent bar before a reveal; thin the band during a reveal so every note is audible.

Foley follows the materials of print, dry and close, no reverb: letterpress clack, ruling pen "tss", guillotine snick, paper slap and slide, numeral thunk, block snap, felt thump for a landing, rubber stamp, typewriter carriage.
pitfalls_limits: Too many thin columns look like a chart → fewer, wider modules.
A "better" composition that isn't obviously better → one strong diagonal with long/short rhythm, a larger signal element, bleeds, type over colour. Merely tilting is not enough.
Rotating and labelling at once reads as noise → rotate, hold, then add labels.
Merged bars show seams after rotation → overdraw 1 px.
Elements that share the camera matrix leak into other shots → draw them only when on screen.
Canvas `letterSpacing` affects `measureText` → measure after setting the font.
Onsets that fall between frames flicker → put visual onsets on whole frames.
Whisper splits or merges words and pads the first word → align by letters, clamp to 0.
styles.engine_section: In `demo/`: `ease.js` (`cubic-bezier(.7,0,.2,1)`, `snap(t, t_arrive, dur)`, `steps()`, `track()`), `film.js` (layout system, clip-reveal text, knife cuts, bars from a score, rotation reveal, wall of artifacts, caption rows), `main.js` (fonts, whisper word times, `?nosub=1`, `?poster=1`), `score.json` (the shared data file for picture and music), `tools/words.py` and `tools/subs.py` (word timings, asserted subtitle intervals). File list and build steps: [DEMO.md](DEMO.md) "Build notes".

styles.name: 60s Spy Title Sequence
styles.official_demo_line: Opening titles for an imaginary 1964 spy film: a chase for a stolen key until the shapes lock into the title.
styles.principles: - Flat, opaque inks on paper: four colours, no gradients. - Hand-cut edges on every shape; pieces layered with cut gaps and small paper shadows. - Abstraction down to silhouettes: figures in profile, all acting in outline and timing. - Typography is the picture's structure: credits are architecture, props, vehicles. - Music cuts the picture: brass stabs are edit points. - A title sequence is a story in itself: one goal, a few locations, one reveal.
construction: Scissor-cut edges: every polygon resampled every ~9–10 px and displaced along its normal by low-frequency noise (amp ~1.2–2.2 px, larger for bigger shapes) plus a rare 1–2 px notch. Cut the edge once in the piece's local space and cache it, so a moving cutout

Paper layering: separate pieces are separated by a ~2.4 px cut gap in the ground colour and cast a small paper shadow (offset a few px, blur ~5, alpha ~0.3). Whole figures get the gap as an outline, so a black figure reads in front of a black letter.
Paper texture: one full-frame texture multiplied on top (mottling + faint fibres), a sparse "ink void" speckle on dark ink, faint squeegee streaks; film grain in the mux (~6).

Silhouette figures: tall stylised adults (~7 heads), identity by hat, coat cut, shoes and one colour accent that doubles as a motion indicator (a tie or scarf streaming back when running). Pieces merge into one outline inside the figure, with only thin slits a
The object of the chase sits on a black backing (an ink keyline) so it reads on any ground; it is the brightest thing in frame.

Type: a condensed OFL display face (e.g. League Gothic) for credits, glyph outlines extracted (opentype.js) and re-cut per letter (edge noise, ±0.8° rotation, ±1.5 px baseline jitter). A title in custom geometric cut glyphs (straight cuts + arcs, uneven weight
colour_logic: Four inks: ink black, paper cream, one hot colour, one warm secondary. Darker "shadow paper" variants of those inks only for depth.
One dominant ground colour per scene, changing with the location; figures and type in the other inks.
The hot colour is reserved for one accent on the hero and for danger; the secondary marks the object of the chase.
Background props go in a darker version of the ground, never in black, or they read as letters.
motion: Puppets on twos (12 fps): poses and positions of figures, hands, letters landing, vehicles. Camera, credit slides and grid growth on ones (24 fps): a stepped camera judders.
Run cycles of ~8 drawings, one step per beat, a strong lean, the accent flying back. Walks one step per beat, coats swinging.
Credits slide in along grid lines and stop dead on the beat (short ease-out); letters land with a paper slap.
Stop-time: at a stab the whole picture freezes (background scroll included) for a couple of beats in total silence, then resumes.
Shattering: a scene sliced into strips parallel to a cut line that slide off alternately along the diagonal.
camera_grammar: Wide on a full credit line, then truck in
Hard cut on a brass stab
Graphic match cut (same shape, same position)
Locked single shape on a flat ground
Vertical pan down a column of type
Push into a letter until it fills frame
sound_palette: 1960s spy big band: stacked staccato trumpets and trombones in octaves with crash (the stab), surf guitar low-string twang through a spring reverb, walking upright bass, brushes or sticks, bongos and shakers, vibraphone, flute, organ stabs, harpsichord. Minor
Stabs = edit points: place staccato brass ~8 ms early so the sample's peak hits the frame.
Techniques (options): a cut interval that shrinks as a chase accelerates; stop-time silence; a big chord for the title followed by a short button; a solo instrument alone for a quiet scene.

Foley follows the material: paper (cut "shh", slides, card slaps for letters landing, blind flips, a tear), metal (keys, chains, locks, clicks), tape (click, hiss). Environments only hinted: a jet pass panned, train wheels in tempo, roulette ticks slowing, win
native_moves: The object of the chase is the title.
pitfalls_limits: Every internal piece outlined with a gap looks like a mannequin diagram → merge pieces in an offscreen layer, cut only joint slits (`destination-out`), outline the whole figure.
A `clear()` that resets the transform silently kills the camera.
A figure fully hidden behind a letter reads as "nobody there" → let hat, nose and accent stick out. A stiff streamer reads as a tongue → multi-segment ribbon with a travelling sine.
A credit only ever seen partially is uncomfortable → always open wide on the full line.
Black background props read as letters → darker ground colour.
An object in the same ink as its ground vanishes → black backing.
Circular props dropped into a word cover neighbouring letters → lay the word out around a gap.
Match cuts fail if circle centres move across the cut.
styles.engine_section: In `demo/`: `paper.js` (four inks, cached scissor edges, cut gaps, paper shadow, texture, silhouette layer with joint slits), `glyph.js` (League Gothic → opentype.js outlines → re-cut letters), `chars.js` (silhouette rigs, poses, run/walk cycles), `title.js` (custom cut title glyphs, diagonal split), `story.js` (tempo grid, single source of timing), `film.js` (timeline, acting, cameras, subtitles, sound events). `?sheet=1` renders a model sheet, `?frame=<scene>` a style frame. File list and build steps: [DEMO.md](DEMO.md) "Build notes".

styles.name: Art Deco
styles.official_demo_line: A grand hotel, 1930: a bellboy races lifts and revolving doors to deliver one letter before midnight.
styles.principles: A world built from gold keylines on warm black, filled with airbrushed hard-edged volumes (Cassandre, Lempicka), organised around one vertical axis. Ornament *is* the picture: sunbursts are backgrounds, stepped arches are frames, a dial is a progress bar, a bulb marquee is a reveal. Motion is mechanical and symmetrical: things unfold from the centre, doors split along the seam, lights switch on in counted order. Native register: glamour with a clock ticking (an event, a deadline, a launch).
construction: Ground: warm lacquer black, never neutral grey-black; a night sky may drift toward a deep emerald near the horizon.
Gold is a banded metal gradient (dark – light – hot – light – dark); animate its `sheen` offset for a light sweep.

The signature stroke (`gline`): a dark engraved underline ~1.6 px wider than the line, the gold gradient line, and a hairline highlight on top. Optional glow and a parallel twin (`double`). Nothing gets a black cartoon outline.
Volumes: hard edge + airbrush (`airbrush`): a directional gradient from shade to light inside the shape, one consistent light direction (upper left by default), a thin gold rim on the lit side.
Motifs (sunburst, stepped arch / ziggurat, fish-scale, chevrons, fan, four-point sparkle, speed lines, clock face, dial) are structural (a background, a frame, a transition), not stickers.
Perspective is real: true one-point (mode-7 floors) and two-point perspective through a pinhole camera, so dolly, tilt and pan change perspective instead of scaling flats.
colour_logic: Three constants: warm black ground, gold line and metal, ivory for paper, gloves, light and type.

One saturated accent reserved for the protagonist (or the one object the story follows). It is the only large saturated area, so the eye finds it in any wide shot. A cooler jewel tone may carry secondary surfaces, never competing in area.
The one-colour exception: any single element can be drawn in its own colour through the same fill + keyline + glow (`color` option) while everything else stays gold.
Always expand hex to six digits in code (three-digit hex breaks colour mixing).
motion: Characters step on twos (12 fps); camera, light, bulbs, gold draw-on and sheen run on ones (24 fps). A stepped camera reads as stutter.
Everything unfolds from the centre: a point → a hairline → bars open symmetrically → text rises → wings and sparkle.
Draw-on follows the music: a gold line grows at the speed of the phrase under it and lands on the hit.
Bulbs have an ignition overshoot (~1.6× flash settling in ~0.18 s) and a relay "chunk"; once a sign is lit, a fast chase may run across it.
Mechanical easing: doors, dials and hands move with firm ease-in-out and a small settle, like machinery; nothing floats.
Performance beats get anticipation and escalation in threes (once, twice, mash).
camera_grammar: Symmetric split (two door leaves hinged at the edges; or a revolving-door wipe)
Leaves sliding shut over the live shot
Architectural section (pull out to a cutaway of the whole building)
Busby Berkeley overhead, mirrored and rotating
Push-in on a dial, medallion or clock
Match-cut on shape (circle → circle, ray → ray)
Low oblique along a sign or marquee
Pull back from detail to skyline
sound_palette: Symphonic jazz of the 1920s–30s, not a 60s big band. Options: stride or concert piano, clarinet (trill; a glissando by time-varying resampling of a long note), strings (tremolo, rushes, pizzicato), muted trumpet commentary, trombone and sax section, walking pi
Rhythm families to choose from: foxtrot, Charleston, tango, a slow torch-song ballad, a fanfare in the manner of a newsreel.

Techniques (options): one hit per unit of counted light; accelerate by dividing the beat; plant a theme in fragments so its full statement is a payoff; low-pass a band that is physically far away and open it as we approach; move a period narrator through acous

Foley by material: brass clicks, bronze clang + chain, iron treads, marble heels, silver trays, wooden doors + spring twang, paper flutter, knife-switch "chunk" + filament hum, relay ticks, elevator ding, champagne cork.
pitfalls_limits: Bulb signs from glyph skeletons break on curves (G, S, R): Zhang–Suen staircase pixels fool a neighbour-count junction test → use the crossing number and weld chain ends within ~14 px.
A generic cartoon character looks pasted in → characters are deco (§2).
Fish-scale reads as brickwork → lower half-circles row by row, each overlapping the previous row, plus an inner arc.
Door leaves over a flat "interior" read as a blank frame → draw only the leaves, closing over the live shot.
A gold point on pure black trips `blackdetect` → lift the background wedges and glow slightly.
Period loudspeaker distortion is unintelligible under music → gentle drive; whisper-check every line on the final mix.
styles.engine_section: Canvas2D, deterministic in `t`, in `demo/engine/`: `deco.js` (gold gradient, `gline`, `airbrush`, motifs, `drawShape` for any path in the deco manner, `color` for the one-colour exception), `type.js` (title bar, digits, badges, dial, clock, `subtitleCard`), `bulbs.js` (any text → bulb sign, `litSequence`), `cam.js` (pinhole camera, `cardTransform`). `demo/frames.js` renders model sheets and style frames from the real engine. Signatures and a minimal example that draws something not in the demo: DEMO.md "Engine reference".

styles.name: Pictogram Motion
styles.official_demo_line: A yellow umbrella left on a bus waits out a sunny day on the lost-property shelf, then opens with 312 others when the storm comes back: objects, vehicles, weather and signs as beat-locked geometric pictograms.
styles.principles: Either a catalogue film: N items (products, dishes, steps, species…) shown one card at a time, fast, on the beat; or a story told in pictograms: one pictogram as the hero (an object, a vehicle, a sign as often as a person), a goal, a turn, an ending, told through the same cards, walls and transitions. Each card = one pictogram doing one action + a huge title + a second-language line + a mono index "07 / N". Cards group into chapters; each chapter owns one hue, opened by a full-bleed pattern card.
construction: Flat Canvas2D, rendered clean; grain only at mux time. One square grid (cell ≈ 1/6 of the frame height) rules bands, transitions and walls.

Pattern model: fill with a mid-dark tone; on grid nodes randomly place cell-radius discs in random tones and discs-with-inner-discs; then a fraction of cells get one motif from a library of generic geometry (quarter-discs, fish-scale waves, dot and triangle sc

Pictogram model: one stroke weight family per film (round caps), solid fills, at most two tones per pictogram (a darker gore, a far side). Objects keep their silhouette at icon size; anything that cannot be read as a sign at 60 px is cut.

Figure model (optional): unit = body height, origin at the hip; draw far limbs (mixed ~40 % toward the background), torso, near limbs, head. A second person sits behind, mixed further (~60 %). People can also appear only through their traces (footprints, a que
Stage: the hero pictogram (any object or figure) sits on a large sun disc in a neighbouring tone, crossed by one faint light sweep.
Environments (water, nets, ramps, rails, rain) live in the hero's own buffer, masked to zero before the text column.
colour_logic: A set of five hues + one dark neutral, each hue in five tones (darkest → lightest, the middle one is the base). A chapter = one hue; a multi-hue chapter rotates through the set per card.
Under type the pattern runs at low contrast; on chapter cards at full contrast.
Light hues take dark type and dark figures, and their disc uses the lighter tone; dark hues take cream. On the dark neutral, the disc uses a lighter tone or it vanishes; its accent is one warm hue.
One cream and one ink serve every hue. No outlines, no highlights except the sweep.
motion: A grid of time: pick one tempo for the film; every shot starts on a beat and every key action in a pose (release, contact, landing) lands on an integer beat.
Pace ladder: normal cards last one bar; related sub-items become half-length rapid-fire runs. A second tempo comes from dividing the beat, never from changing tempo.
Easing: exponential ease-out for entrances, exponential in-out for whips and wipes; a back ease once at most.
Type enters by mask slide-up: title first, second line ~0.08 s later, tag after; meta lines type on without a caret. Short cards compress all timings.
Pictogram assembly: the hero pictogram and its stage arrive as horizontal bands sliding into register from alternating sides.
Backgrounds breathe: rows drift in alternating directions; on chapter cards they jump a quarter-cell on beats.
camera_grammar: Lateral track with a one-screen whip per beat
Push into one motif cell until it becomes the next frame
Pull back to a tiled wall of items
Split screen along a grid line
sound_palette: Type and music can carry the film alone; a voice is optional, calm, one or two lines per chapter.
Percussion is the spine: choose a drum family that suits the topic (frame drums, taiko, marching snares, steel pans, body percussion, an electronic kit) plus rim clicks, claps, shakers and crashes.

Colour instruments on top: Karplus-Strong plucks (any lute, koto or harp-like voice, with pitch bends), mallets (marimba, glockenspiel), detuned-saw chord stabs, a synth bass, pads, risers and a drone.
Per-family accents: every shot onset gets a hit chosen by chapter (a splash, a pok, a clank, a crack, a whoosh, a sizzle): foley reads the chapter's matter.
pitfalls_limits: Figure environments spread into the text column → render the figure layer into its own buffer and fade it out with a gradient mask before the text.
Cream on light hues fails contrast → dark type and dark figures on light hues; their disc is the lighter tone.
The sun disc vanishes on the dark neutral → use a lighter tone for it.
Pattern canvases are large and seeded per card → cache with a bounded LRU; an unbounded cache runs out of memory with parallel renderers.
Horizontal poses (swimming, lying, crawling) cross the title → move the stage outward and narrow the text column.
Imitating a real identity too closely → your own palette, mark and slogan from the grid motifs.
styles.engine_section: In `demo/`: `engine.js` (palette, `G.pattern` / `G.drawPattern` with whole-row offsets, `G.motif`, pictograms such as `G.umbrella`, `G.drop`, `G.cloud`, `G.sunIcon`, `G.moon`, `G.bolt`, `G.foot`, `G.item`, `G.maskText`, easings), `film.js` (shot list in film seconds, sound events, scenes, HUD, captions, grid transitions, motion blur), `mix.py` (picture-locked score, foley and voice from the same events). API table and a minimal example: [DEMO.md](DEMO.md#engine-reference).

styles.name: Bauhaus Shapes
styles.official_demo_line: One dot doubles every ten years: 128 after seventy, 6.02 without compounding, and the last ten years are worth all the rest.
styles.principles: - Shapes are amounts. A disc that doubles doubles its *area* (radius × √2); a weight three times heavier is a square of three times the area; a share of a whole is a ring of that share of the area. If the numbers would make a shape unreadably small, change the framing, never the proportions. - Shapes have roles. Circle = what grows or moves; square = what stays or weighs; triangle = slope, time, pivot. One shape keeps one meaning through a film. - Point → line → plane. The protagonist starts as a dot, draws a line by moving (its path stays on screen), and becomes a plane (a field, a disc that
construction: Canvas 2D, flat fills, hard edges. No gradients, shadows, glows, transparency between shapes, outlines on filled shapes or rounded rectangles.

Opaque ink on matte card. One full-frame finish pass: fine paper tooth and fibre (about ±7 levels, a touch more in dark inks) and a very slow, barely visible ink-density drift inside colour fields. Edges stay sharp; no misregistration, no ageing, no halftone.
Lines: one weight for paths (5 px), one for construction and leaders (2–3 px), butt caps. Lines only draw a path, a tangent, a leader or the grid; never a decorative frame.
Compass marks: a small cross at the centre a circle was drawn from may stay visible; it is the Vorkurs construction layer, not decoration.
Cropping is tension: big discs and slopes run out of frame. Anything being compared is fully in frame.
colour_logic: No pure black, no dark ground. Ink is a deep blue-black used only for line and type.
Reversed type on a field uses the paper colour, so protagonist and field must be dark enough to carry it.
A palette swap changes nothing but these six values.

Example palettes (our demo): Klein paper #F8F7F3, protagonist #0E9F7A, field #2138C8, pivot #F4E04D, secondary #D5DCEE, ink #161C3A; Sorbet paper #F5E8E1, protagonist #E9476B, field #3552E8, pivot #F6B12F, secondary #94D3BF, ink #1F3340.
motion: Roll: pure rolling, angular speed = distance ÷ radius, so the path is a true cycloid. A growing ball's phase is integrated along the path.
Grow: at each step a ring lands on the outside ("thunk"), newest outermost, all rings tangent at the protagonist's core.
Land: squares slide along the grid and lock with a small overshoot; slopes swing up about one corner; dots drop and squash once.
Sweep: a turning thing leaves a secondary-colour wedge; the same angle sweeps more area at a larger radius.
Cut: a shape is circled with a compass stroke, then lifted out, leaving a paper hole; tangents connect the hole to the piece.
Retract: construction lines shrink from one end to the other; nothing fades out.
sound_palette: Score: light tuned percussion and plucked strings (marimba, vibraphone, kalimba, harp, pizzicato) on a steady grid; chords land with each completed shape.

Effects follow the geometry: a ruling-pen hiss for each grid line, wooden clacks for squares locking, low thuds for slopes and drops (lower as a ball gets bigger), a kalimba note per ring climbing the scale, a whoosh for whips and swings.
With a voice: compress it, sit the bed about 10 dB under it by RMS, dip the music in 300 Hz–4 kHz while a line plays.
styles.engine_section: - Topics: mechanisms that reduce to geometry (levers, gears, pulleys, supply and demand, orbits), shares and growth, titles and chapter cards. - Palettes: any six-colour set that keeps the roles and a light ground. - Length: from a 10-second title to a 50-second explainer; a voice is optional, the shapes must read without it. - Still layouts work as well (title, mechanism, data): `demo/index.html?frame=1|2|3`.

styles.name: Scale Zoom Explainer
styles.official_demo_line: A little probe whose eye is a zoom lens fires a dotted sight line at each next stop and takes us from the Milky Way down to a virus.
styles.principles: - Flat and opaque: every object is a solid colour plus at most one shade step. No gradients, blur, transparency, outlines or drop shadows. - Glow is two hard rings: anything bright sits on two concentric solid discs one and two steps lighter than the night ground, like a screen print. - True scale inside each frame, a readout for the camera: things in one frame are drawn to one scale; a corner ribbon (a log track with a few stop icons) and a field-of-view number come from the same camera. - A guide with a lens for an eye: a round, friendly character whose single eye is a zoom lens. Where it lo
construction: SVG, rebuilt every frame from a pure function of time; every random draw from a fixed seed. Nothing is carried from the previous frame.

One shade step: draw the whole shape in the shade colour, then the base colour on a copy shifted toward the light (upper left) and clipped to the shape; what is left is a crescent at the lower right. Land, clouds and anything on a sphere follow the sphere's te
Forms: circles, ellipses, rounded rectangles and smooth closed curves (Catmull-Rom). Thin lines are round-capped and 2.5–4 px.
Stars: three colours of dots (mist, cream, sun) and a few four-point sparkles. Dots never flicker; sparkles may breathe slowly (±16 %, ~0.3 Hz, each on its own phase).
Grain: none in video (a static grain sits on moving shapes; a moving grain makes flat fields shimmer). A 5 % static grain is allowed on still frames only.

One camera, screen = (p − C)·z + S0, with parallax layers taking a fraction of the zoom (stars ~0.18, far objects ~0.4, the subject ~0.75, the guide 1.0). Everything that follows a subject (sight line ends, rings, labels) goes through that function. Zooms inte
colour_logic: Ground: a deep night blue; its two lighter steps are reserved for glow rings and dim shapes.

Five hues, each with one shade step: a blue (oceans, arms, nuclei, glass), a mint (land, living cells, one orbit), a coral (bacteria, blood, the guide's cheeks, one orbit), a sun yellow (the guide's body, every "pointer": dots, rings, tape, progress, sign-off)
Sun yellow means *look here*. It is never a background.
No pure black, pure white or grey.
motion: 24 fps, every frame on ones; the camera and the guide move smoothly every frame.

Performance: anticipation, action, overshoot and settle on every meaningful move (squash before a jump, stretch on release, panels flapping like ears, the antenna bead lagging half a beat). Poses blend by easing, never by switching in an `if`.

The eye carries the face: a lid for blinks, the iris itself bending into an upward arch for a smile (never a colour block over the lens), the iris widening for surprise, the barrel stepping out with turning grooves for a zoom.
Dots of a sight line pop out one by one (0 → 1.3 → 1), then stream slowly toward the target, growing in at the start and shrinking out at the end.
Rings lock with a spring (one overshoot); counters roll and land.
Never moves: subtitles once landed, the corner instrument's position.
camera_grammar: Log-space dolly through a shape (ring, lens, iris)
Pull back from an extreme close-up
Tracking with a moving thing while pulling out
Shape match (a small dot becomes the next subject)
sound_palette: Tuned percussion and plucks: vibraphone (soft and bowed), glockenspiel, marimba, xylophone, harp, hand chimes; pizzicato strings and double bass; nylon guitar for warm human-scale moments; timpani and triangle for locks.

Foley of a small machine: servo whirrs for the lens, a shutter click for blinks, soft puffs and a low thruster bed, rising blips for each dot of a sight line, a click and a short bell when a ring locks, whooshes for dives.

Option for colour per level: the same key and tempo throughout, a different lead instrument for each scale (bowed pad in space, marimba on Earth, guitar on a hand, pizzicato in minor inside a body, bells for the very small).
Silence: a held half-beat before a release, and one near-silence before the smallest reveal.
pitfalls_limits: Readable scale: things too small to see at true scale become markers (a dot with a ring); say so with a label. Never enlarge a true-scale thing to fit the composition: change the level instead.
The guide's size: viewers read it as information. State once that it is drawn larger than life, show its true size once, and say when it shrinks along.
A flat face: covering the lower half of a lens eye with a colour block reads as sleepy or hurt; bend the iris instead.
Light grounds: cream text and cream skin collide; put subtitles and the corner instrument on an opaque night plate there.
Overshoot of a pull-back reveals the edge of the star field: lay stars beyond the frame.
Shimmer: small dots moving sub-pixel are fine; random per-frame twinkle is not.
Hands and props drawn as plain capsules read as extra fingers: draw curled fingers, a thumb and a knuckle line.
styles.engine_section: - `demo/flat.js`: palette `C`, `shaded()` (one shade step), `twoTone()` (terminator for land and clouds), `halo()` (two hard rings), `stars()`, `sparkle()`, `blobPath()`, `text()` (records labels for `window.TEXTS`). - `demo/orbi.js`: `orbi(p, x, y, s, P)` with continuous pose parameters (`look`, `lid`, `smile`, `zoom`, `wide`, `sq`, `tilt`, `ant`, `flame`, `hold`) and `orbiLens()` for the sight line's origin. - `demo/film.js`: camera with parallax layers (`camAt`, `layerOf`), easing helpers (`kf`, `spr`, `wob`), `wipeText()`, the first performance. - `demo/scenes.js`: `ringAt()` (next-stop ri

styles.name: Text Flash Cuts
styles.official_demo_line: A letter, a phone call, a wall of windows, thirteen steps: the girl who told him not to look back is always one step closer, until she turns her head.
styles.principles: Three layers, and the collision between them is the look: - Type as picture. A word fills the frame, bleeds off an edge, or stands in a vertical column. Cards are dialogue, chapter titles and punctuation of the cut. - Symbolic architecture. Stairs that never end, window grids, lockers, a one-point street: flat polygons, no props, no sky, no texture. - Flat characters in three states only: black silhouette (far), flat cel colour (mid), fragment (an eye, a hand, a mouth corner) filling the frame.
construction: Characters: generated cel art, clean thin uniform black lines, completely flat fills with a single hard shadow tone, no gradients, no paper grain. Keyed from a chroma-green background into RGBA; any pure generated red is pulled to the film's red.
Everything code-drawn is hard-edged polygons on Canvas 2D. No blur, no glow, no grain (mux grain 0). The only smear is the head-tilt ghosting (three 28 % copies of the head layer).
Silhouettes are the same art filled with one colour (`source-in`), so a character can be black, white or red without new images.
colour_logic: Inversion is red-black swapping, never RGB inversion (RGB inversion makes cyan): grayscale → contrast(5) → invert → multiply red. White becomes black, black becomes red. Used as 1–6-frame accents on impacts, never as a look.

Each speaker owns a field colour (for example: protagonist = red rail, black type; second character = black rail, white type). Keep it fixed through the film so the audience reads who speaks without voices.
motion: Editing is the animation: flash cards 2–9 frames at 30 fps; architecture shots 0.3–1.6 s; nothing static for more than a second. Lock cuts to a beat grid (150 BPM = 12 frames a beat works well at 30 fps; 8th = 6 frames, 16th = 3 frames).
Card slam: frame 0 at 1.08×, frame 1 at 1.02×, then 1.0; jitter 10–14 px on the first two frames, 1–3 px after (whole-pixel random per frame, no motion blur).
Rails slam in from the frame edge in 3 frames and are counted as on screen only when complete.
Characters move by layers and steps, not tweens: a head layer rotated about the neck, a figure that jumps closer once per beat, a silhouette that bobs once per step.
Accelerate by shortening shots (9 → 6 → 4 → 3 frames), not by moving faster.
camera_grammar: Fast push into a one-point corridor, stairs or street, perfectly symmetric
Extreme offset: subject at one edge, half the frame empty
Hard push into one element of a grid (a locker, a window)
Lateral track along an orthogonal wall
Beat-locked step push (the camera jumps one step per beat)
Low angle from below a figure at the top of a space
Insert at 1:1 scale (an eye, a hand, a letter) held under a slow push
Multi-panel grid of one face cropped many ways
Split frame: picture on one side, a speaker's rail on the other
sound_palette: Instruments: harpsichord ostinato in 16ths, contrabass and cello pizzicato, a woodblock as a clock, glockenspiel for a lullaby motif, violins tremolo at a whisper, bowed vibraphone, timpani, bass drum, snare, low brass (trombone, tuba, horn) for stabs and a ♭9
Card hit (synthesised): high-passed noise transient + metallic ring at 1760/2637/4186 Hz + a 52 Hz drop; pitch rises card by card as tension rises.
Foley: locker clank, paper, phone vibration (155 Hz gated square), footsteps that grow louder, a weather bed, a neck-bone "crack" (low clack + click + noise transient) for the head tilt, heartbeat.
Silence is a cut: at least two hard silences (a gate on everything but one sound), the longest right before the head tilt.
styles.engine_section: - RGB inversion turns red cyan → red-black swap (§3). - A large head rotation shows a gap at the neck → only rotate far while the figure is a silhouette; in colour stay within 0.1 rad. - A black silhouette in a black doorway disappears → doorways are white. - A half-body image standing in a long shot "breaks at the waist" → generate a full-body back view for long shots. - Flash cards counted as dialogue fail the reading check, and cutting away from a held line resets its clock → hold lines on rails or objects while the picture beside them cuts. - Centred cards on plain fields read as slides →

styles.name: Silhouette Rhythm
styles.official_demo_line: A flock of flamingos moves on every beat, and one young bird is always half a beat late; the ripples the others left on the water teach it the beat.
styles.principles: - The figure is one black shape. No detail inside it, no gradient, no outline, no shadow. Everything the viewer reads is in the contour. - There is always light behind it: the sun disc, the bright band of the horizon, the glitter on the water. A silhouette sits on light, never on dark. - Poses land on the beat and hold between beats. A group moves in unison; anything off the beat is a deliberate choice of the story. - The freeze: on the key beat the figures, droplets, ripples and clouds stop; the sky's colour and the sun keep going. - The sky is the clock: the colour sinks from gold to magenta
construction: Three 2D layers composited in one fragment shader: silhouettes, their reflections, water light (ripples and droplets). The shader paints the sky, the sun and the water, then lays the layers over it.

Sky: two vertical colour ramps (gold-to-crimson and magenta-to-violet) blended by one story-phase value; perspective cloud streaks lit on their sun-facing edge; a sun disc with a warm glow and a horizontal flare band.

Water: the sky reflected with wobble from two noise octaves anchored to the world, a glitter column under the sun, darker towards the camera. Reflections of figures are the same shapes flipped about the waterline, wobbled and darkened.
Light around the figures: volumetric rays marched from each pixel toward the sun (56 steps) and occluded by the silhouettes; a thin rim on the sun-facing edge and a soft halo, stronger near the sun.

Ripples have a bright crest (in the water-light layer, tinted by the sky) and a dark trough (in the reflection layer), so they read on bright and dark water alike. Droplets are bright beads, never black specks.
Camera: a level pinhole over flat water (focal length, horizon height, camera height, lateral and depth offset, yaw). Long focal lengths make the sun huge; the horizon height frames the shot.
colour_logic: Two values carry the frame: black figure and bright ground. Everything else is the sky's gradient.
The figure colour is fixed: near-black with a trace of violet. It never takes a hue.
The sky moves through warm hues only (gold, orange, coral, crimson, magenta, violet). No green, no blue sky, no grey.
Brightest values belong to the sun, the horizon band and the light on the water; type uses the sun's cream, never pure white.
motion: 30 fps, everything on ones. Poses snap into place in ~0.13 s with a small overshoot (ease-out-back) and hold until the next beat.
Feet stay planted in the world while walking or running (two-bone IK); never slide a standing figure.
Wings, steps and head turns are scheduled on the beat grid: the top of a wingbeat, a footfall, a head flag on the beat; double-time subdivision for running.
The freeze stops subject time and the shader's noise time together; only the sky phase and the sun height continue. A camera may move inside a frozen moment.
Never moves: the horizon line within a shot (no dutch tilt), the sun's place in the world.
camera_grammar: Telephoto, sun filling half the frame
Low lateral track at water level
sound_palette: Instruments: tuned wood and metal percussion (marimba, kalimba, vibraphone, glockenspiel), plucked bass, a dry kit, claps and shakers; strings only for held chords under a freeze.
Character sounds are rhythm: each kind of figure owns one percussive voice (a low log drum, a bright woodblock…) that lands where its gesture lands. Being on or off the beat is audible.
Foley: water in all sizes (step, patter, splash, plop, drip), wing pushes, distant calls, wind. Footfalls pan with position.
Silence as a tool: cut the music dead (a record stop, a half-beat drop) before the turn and before the climax; keep only water and wind. The first sound after the silence is the most important one.
native_moves: The beat written on the water.
The freeze with the sky still moving.
pitfalls_limits: Black on dark. A silhouette over dark water or a violet zenith disappears. Put it in the glitter column, against the horizon band or in front of the sun.
Merged shapes. Overlapping figures become one blob; at key moments leave air between contours and keep limbs in profile.
Unreadable spread shapes. Open wings or limbs seen face-on lose the species or the person. Prefer profile; for birds, show flight from the side (neck forward, legs back), not a V above the body.
Puppet humans. A naive forward-kinematics human reads as a marionette. Hand-key a small set of anatomically correct poses and blend them, or use animals.
Tiny subject in the wide. If the subject must be small, make that the point (solitude) and keep it on light; otherwise cut closer.
Blocky blur. Never fake motion blur by downscaling and upscaling the frame; sample along the motion at full resolution.
Cutting on every beat. The beat lives in the poses; cuts follow sections.
styles.engine_section: - `demo/sky.js` — `SKY.make(canvas)` returns `draw(P, [silhouettes, reflections, waterLight])`: the sky, sun, water, rays, rim and halo shader. Parameters: `hor`, `fpx`, `yaw`, `cx`, `ch` (camera), `sun`, `sunR`, `ph` (colour phase 0 → 1), `vs` (gradient compression for long lenses), `pulse` (beat glow), `flash`, `rays`, `T` (noise time; hold it to freeze). - `demo/shapes.js` — parametric silhouettes in local metres (the demo's cast; your film builds its own): `flamingo(ctx, P, seed)` (standing and walking: body spline, Bézier neck tube, head with bent bill, two-bone legs; `juv` for a young bi

styles.name: Blueprint
styles.official_demo_line: An inventor's blueprint draws, explodes and assembles a cloud-catching machine, and its revision cloud starts to rain.
styles.principles: - The whole film happens on one sheet of blueprint paper lying on a dark drafting table. The camera moves over it like an eye reading a drawing. - White line work on uneven Prussian blue: centre lines, outlines, hatching, dimension lines, leader lines with numbered balloons, a title block, a notes column. - A 2D line-drawing language: orthographic and oblique/isometric projection are allowed, 3D rendering never. - Rigorous convention carries the tone: the drawing is dry and exact; the notes can carry wit, warmth or gravity. - The designed thing is the character. A machine, object, building or
construction: Sheet: procedural cyanotype in a shader in *sheet coordinates*, crisp at any zoom: fbm between two Prussian blues, coating streaks, fibres, fold creases (bright edge, dark edge, whitening), bleached edges, specks. Around it: dark drafting cloth with a drop sha

Lines: pale blue-white, slightly soft (mipmap bleed), a faint ink breakup driven by paper grain. Four weights (outline, detail, thin, hair; e.g. 3.2 / 2.0 / 1.25 / 0.9 sheet units). Screen width = sheet width × zoom^0.65, so close-ups don't turn into sausages
Dash conventions: centre line (long-short), hidden (short dashes), phantom / cutting plane (long-short-short), scaled with zoom so the pattern stays on the paper.

Occlusion by painter's order: every solid is filled with "paper" before its outline is stroked. Oblique extrusion: stroke the outline at N depth steps at 2× width, then fill the same steps with paper; a clean silhouette survives.

Composite in buffers: ink (white = exposed line); fx (shadow, wetness, stamp ink as channels); a subtitle overlay last. Shadows darken lines too: that is how a lifted object proves it has left the paper.
Hatching (fine-line shading) for sections, soil, weights, at 45°, spacing 8–14 units.
colour_logic: Blue and white only. The blue varies in value (coating, stains, folds); the white varies in weight and softness, never in hue.
One non-blue colour, used exactly once: a rubber-stamp ink (red is classic; a green APPROVED or black VOID work too). It carries the verdict.
The "real" object at the climax may carry light (white glow, soft value), not a new hue.
Example blues: `#18336B` → `#2A58A6` with lines `#E7F0F9` and table `#0D1116`; a faded sun-bleached sheet `#3A6DA8` → `#5B8CC4`; a deep over-exposed sheet `#0F2350` → `#1D3F80`.
motion: Camera and draw-on on ones (24 fps). Continuous moves within a section, hard cuts on downbeats between sections; tiny camera bumps only for physical impacts (paper slap, stamp).
Draw-on truncated by arc length with a glowing nib at the head; items staggered within a layer; each layer starts on a beat.
Drafting order: centre lines → outlines → detail → hatching → dimensions → balloons → labels.
Exploded views: parts leave in sequence on subdivisions of the beat, eased, and return one per beat-group with a click.
Mechanisms step on the grid like an escapement: a gear advances one tooth per subdivision with a short ease-out; meshing phases computed so teeth really interlock; chains move with their sprockets.
Machine acting: angles, droops, volumes and gauge needles are the face. Failure = slowing, sagging, winding down over ~1.5 s; joy = snapping upright, a needle overshooting (back-ease).
camera_grammar: Medium on a figure, subject ~80 % of height, sky on one side
Track along a path of force (chain, pipe, wire, beam)
Lateral pan across Fig. 1 → Fig. 2 → Fig. 3
sound_palette: Contrapuntal, mechanical music: harpsichord, bassoon, strings spiccato, harp, celesta, music box, clavichord, a small wind ensemble. Imitative lines (an invention, a canon, a fugato) feel like interlocking parts; a short repeated motive can be the "gear".

Foley follows materials. Paper: roll crackle and slap, T-square wood slide, technical pen scratch (2–6 kHz grain, length = stroke length), lettering bursts, compass squeak, hatching strokes, eraser rub, tracing-paper rustle. Brass and wood: part clicks (resona

Options for the arc (in any order, use what the story needs): instruments dropping out with a written-out ritardando into true silence; a single questioning figure alone; a suspended chord held without resolution under the magic; a full cadence on the stamp; t
Silence may contain paper sounds only.
pitfalls_limits: Main figure near the sheet edge → wides show the desk. Keep margins or enlarge the sheet.
Upward explosions hit the header → explode sideways and flatten long parts during the explode.
Subtitles on the ink buffer vanish off-sheet and can't occlude lines → separate overlay, premultiplied alpha.
An object darkened by its own shadow → zero the shadow channel only in its area.
Per-lobe shading on a blobby shape reads as grapes → one gradient across the union; crescents from a union-minus-shifted mask; fill unions as one path (`nonzero`) or overlapping fills make bubbles.
A small payoff undersells the return → the payoff object ~⅓ of frame height, centred, drawn stroke by stroke, subtitles off it.
Line weights not scaled with zoom → sausages in close-ups, vanishing wides.
styles.engine_section: `demo/paper.js` (WebGL2 compositor: procedural cyanotype, ink bleed, wet stains, shadows, stamp, roll), `demo/draw.js` (drafting engine: camera, oblique projection, draw-on polylines, solids with paper fill, hatching, dimensions, balloons, text), `demo/sheet.js` (border, header, title block, parts list, notes, revision cloud, rain, hand shadow, stamp), `demo/film.js` (timeline on a beat grid: cameras, acting, subtitles, sound events). A new machine goes in its own module like `demo/machine.js`. File map and build: [DEMO.md](DEMO.md#build-notes).

styles.name: Isometric Infographic
styles.official_demo_line: A coffee's journey from the plantation to your hands, across one isometric world.
styles.principles: - Flat, true isometric. No perspective, no outlines on solids; shapes are separated only by the three tones of each face. The projection never rotates or tilts. - Infographic furniture is part of the picture: leader lines, label pins, dashed cut lines, hatched section faces, tracking rings, a legend, a route line all live in the world. - Numbers are built from icons (Isotype), and they add up. - A diorama: the system sits on a floating board or plinth with a visible cross-section at its edges, on a pale ground.
construction: Projection: axes at 30°. `sx = (x − y)·cos30°·k`, `sy = ((x + y)·½ − z)·k`; x runs down-right, y down-left, z up; painter depth = x + y + z. Everything is queued and depth-sorted, then flushed.

Three tones per face chosen from its normal: top light, left (+y) mid, right (+x) dark. Derive tones from one base colour: mix toward warm white ~20 % for the top and toward a cool dark (e.g. `#231A2C`) ~22 % for the dark side, so shadows are slightly cool.
Ink lines (2 px) only for infographic elements: leaders, pins, cut lines, rings, routes, labels.
The board: floats on a pale background with a faint isometric dot lattice and a soft blurred shadow; its front faces show strata (soil, water column, floors, pipes) where the section meets the edge.
Composites (a terraced hill with shrubs, a crane over a ship) are drawn as one ordered item or given a depth bias; generic painter sorting fails on them.
People: minimal billboards (round head, tapered two-tone body, a thick arm stroke, a hat or hair shape for identity, no faces), stepping at 12 fps.
colour_logic: A pale neutral ground (cream, paper grey or pale blue) and 5–7 flat hues, each with its three tones; one ink colour.
Colour codes meaning, the way a legend does: one hue per material or role (water is always the same blue, the subject always its hue). Never reuse a hue for two meanings.
The subject's hue is reserved: when the story needs "this one", everything else desaturates toward warm grey and only the subject keeps its colour (focus + context).
Stations that must be found in a wide shot get a pale plate with a dashed ink outline plus one accent hue.
motion: Nothing moves without a line leading it: a route line is drawn slightly ahead, a leader grows before an inset opens, a cut line draws before a skin slides away.
Cutaway: cut line (~0.3 s) → the near skin slides out along its normal and fades (~0.35 s, ease-out) → hatched section rims fade in over the last part.
Isotype fill: icons pop with a back-ease (overshoot), one per subdivision of the beat; count-up numbers run over the same span.

Accumulation = acceleration: arrivals on quarter notes, then eighths, then waves; the eye feels the system taking over. Solids arrive by motion, never by alpha (semi-transparent blocks look like ghosts).
Objects perform: squash on landing (~18 %) and small bounces; colour changes that show a process (raw → cooked, empty → full).
Vehicles follow polylines with ease-in-out and face their tangent.
sound_palette: Music: acoustic and light: kalimba, marimba, nylon guitar, pizzicato, woodblock and hand percussion (shaker, bongo, cajon), upright or synth bass, glockenspiel, toy piano, or a clean electronic pulse for technical systems. A short motif can mark the subject ea

Techniques (options): one sound per icon as numbers fill; instruments dropping out and a low-pass closing as the camera dives; J-cuts (the next station's sound 0.5 s before it appears); one note per station during a final pull-back.
Ambience beds per station, crossfaded (wind and birds, harbour, sea, city hum, machine room, crowd murmur).

Foley by material: fibre snap, fleshy thud, grains pouring, granular rattles, inharmonic steel partials for containers, paper tear, ceramic plink, liquid pour with rising pitch, servo whine, keyboard clicks.
pitfalls_limits: Newell normals depend on vertex order: faces get culled as back faces → give every face an outward hint and flip the normal to match before culling.
Painter sorting breaks on composites → draw them as one ordered item; add depth bias for overhangs.
Semi-transparent moving solids look like ghosts → motion only, no alpha.
A hull or wheel touching the wrong surface reads as an accident → leave visible clearance.
World geometry behind a close-up becomes giant discs → skip detail above a zoom threshold, paint a flat backdrop behind hero layers.
A pull-out through a tall object gives one ugly frame → fade tall objects in by zoom.
Hidden jumps (a time or place change during a dive) must be drawn in screen space anchored on the tracked subject, so the frame doesn't reveal the jump.
An object drawn with the wrong silhouette reads as something else (a white box with a red roof is a house) → give machines their tell-tale parts.
styles.engine_section: `demo/engine.js` is dependency-free Canvas 2D: `Iso` (projection, camera, depth-sorted queue: `box`, `prism`, `cyl`, `cone`, `roof`, `sphere`, `flat`, `line3`, `bill`, `text3`, `push/pop` local frames, `desat` + `keep` one-colour hook), `tri()` three-tone generator, `pin`, `inset`, `cutLine`, `hatch`, `ring`, `ICON.*` + `iconGrid`, `person`, and `shape()` which turns any 2D outline into a shaded isometric solid.
